record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a stronger, more negative dependency score than the comparator; for direction +1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means weaker dependency. For direction -1 interactions, a positive estimate would mean the exposed-group contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement.   H2 (R108), H5 (R109), and H11 (R110) tested MYC amplification on DHX9, KIF18A, and RPL11 dependency. The signed estimates were -0.003, +0.006, and -0.012 respectively, all close to zero and all interval-compatible with no effect. These are far below the practical null scale I am using for dependency scores and do not support MYC amplification as a main predictor of these three outcomes in this dataset. I reject and close all three.   H121 (R111), H122 (R112), H123 (R113), and H124 (R114) tested specificity or pleiotropy of accepted axes. PTEN loss had essentially no association with ERBB2 dependency (-0.002; interval -0.026 to +0.022) or EGFR dependency (+0.006; interval -0.017 to +0.029). KEAP1 loss had only a small positive association with STAT3 dependency (+0.016; interval -0.012 to +0.044), and TP53 wild-type versus loss had only a small positive association with STAT3 dependency (+0.012; interval -0.012 to +0.037). None are statistically significant or practically meaningful, and none undermine the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, or TP53-status axes. I reject and close these specificity checks.   H125 (R115) tested whether KRAS mutation is associated with stronger BRAF dependency among BRAF wild-type cells. The estimate was +0.015 with interval -0.003 to +0.034. It is small and not statistically supported. H126 (R116) tested whether BRAF V600E is associated with weaker RIT1 dependency among KRAS wild-type cells; the signed estimate was +0.013 with interval -0.021 to +0.047, again null. I reject and close both MAPK-bypass relationships.   H127 (R117) and H128 (R118) tested cognate receptor dependencies among adenocarcinoma cells that are KRAS wild-type. ERBB2 amplification gave a small negative signed estimate -0.020 with interval -0.058 to +0.018; EGFR amplification gave +0.019 with interval -0.018 to +0.055. Neither reaches a meaningful magnitude or excludes zero. I reject and close both. These negative results remain dataset-level specificity checks, not proof that receptor amplification cannot matter in other settings.   The key new result is H132 (R119): CDKN2A loss versus no CDKN2A loss on MDM2 dependency. Under the registered direction -1 hypothesis of stronger MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells, the signed estimate is +0.117 with 95% interval +0.082 to +0.152. This corresponds to an approximately 0.117 score-unit shift toward more negative MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. On the MDM2 outcome scale, this is roughly a 40-50% difference relative to the overall mean absolute dependency magnitude and about half a standard deviation, so it is much larger than the near-null effects seen elsewhere in this iteration and crosses the 10% practical-significance threshold by the stated convention.   However, this is still a new discovery after many comparisons and has clear potential confounders. CDKN2A deletion lies in a 9p21 locus that often co-occurs with MTAP deletion, and CDKN2A status is correlated with TP53 pathway alterations; MDM2 biology is strongly p53-pathway-related. Therefore I do not accept H132 immediately. I request independent validation of H132 and register follow-up tests stratified by TP53 status, including the effect of TP53 wild-type versus loss on MDM2 within CDKN2A contexts; MTAP-loss main effect and CDKN2A effect stratified by MTAP status; CDKN2A effect among higher-Cas9 screens to reduce screen-quality confounding; and a specificity test of CDKN2A loss on USP7 dependency, expected potentially opposite if the axis is tied to p53 pathway status. H132 is kept unresolved and active pending validation and follow-up.   The lower-priority untested claims H129, H130, H131, and H133 are deferred because the CDKN2A-MDM2 signal, if validated, is more informative for allocation of remaining work. All conclusions remain dataset-level associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator. For direction +1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For direction -1 interactions, a positive estimate means the exposed-group contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. New validation decisions: H132 is accepted. CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in discovery with a signed estimate of +0.117 and a 95% interval of +0.082 to +0.152. Independent validation reproduced the effect at +0.100 with an independent interval of +0.049 to +0.151, excluding null even after accounting for the validation multiplicity. The magnitude is approximately 0.4 standard deviations of the MDM2 dependency distribution and, using the typical absolute MDM2 dependency magnitude as a rough denominator, corresponds to a change well above the 10% clinical-significance threshold. Therefore the evidence supports a dataset-level association between CDKN2A loss and stronger MDM2 dependency. This remains an association, not a causal or externally generalizable claim, and the remaining TP53, MTAP, and specificity follow-ups are important for interpreting the mechanism. H103 is rejected. The median IFN-gamma interaction for PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency had a small positive discovery estimate, +0.115 with interval +0.012 to +0.219, but independent validation was negative and null-compatible, -0.046 with interval -0.200 to +0.109. The independent interval excludes the discovery point estimate and provides no support for interaction. This is consistent with H92, where the top-quartile IFN interaction also failed to replicate cleanly. The robust conclusion is a main PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency, without reliable IFN context modification. Current supported dataset associations: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma and several context checks; TP53 wild-type status is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency broadly and in many contexts, including validated PIK3CA-mutant cells; and CDKN2A loss is newly supported as associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. These are scientifically meaningful magnitudes compared with the near-null genotype and receptor effects observed across the run. Important negative and specificity findings include: KRAS mutation is not associated with KRAS dependency or with several MAPK-related dependencies after validation; EGFR amplification is not a robust predictor of EGFR or STAT3 dependency after validation; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with ERBB2 or STAT3 dependency; MYC amplification is not associated with DHX9, KIF18A, or RPL11 dependency; PTEN loss is not associated with ERBB2 or EGFR dependency; KEAP1 loss is not associated with STAT3 dependency; TP53 wild-type status is not associated with STAT3 dependency; and most tested interactions, especially IFN-gamma interactions, do not replicate. These negative results support pathway specificity rather than a broad cell-line dependency-state association. Unresolved uncertainty is concentrated on the newly accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association and its potential confounders: CDKN2A deletion can co-occur with MTAP deletion and p53-pathway alterations, and the main effect could be diluted or modified by those factors. The next most informative work is to analyze the active follow-up claims testing CDKN2A-MDM2 within TP53 wild-type and TP53-loss strata, TP53 effects within CDKN2A strata, MTAP-loss main effects and CDKN2A-by-MTAP stratification, a higher-Cas9-quality screen context, a histology context, and specificity against SMARCA2 and USP7 dependency. If the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect remains after MTAP and TP53 stratification and is not mirrored by strong broad copy-number-like effects on unrelated dependencies, it should be treated as a more robust internal p53-axis association. If the effect disappears in MTAP-deleted or TP53-loss contexts, the interpretation should shift toward a stratified or confounded association. No further validation is needed immediately because H132 already has independent validation; remaining validation capacity should be reserved for a future context-specific finding if one emerges.

For direction -1 interactions, a positive estimate means the exposed-group contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. New validation decisions: H132 is accepted. CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in discovery with a signed estimate of +0.117 and a 95% interval of +0.082 to +0.152. Independent validation reproduced the effect at +0.100 with an independent interval of +0.049 to +0.151, excluding null even after accounting for the validation multiplicity. The magnitude is approximately 0.4 standard deviations of the MDM2 dependency distribution and, using the typical absolute MDM2 dependency magnitude as a rough denominator, corresponds to a change well above the 10% clinical-significance threshold. Therefore the evidence supports a dataset-level association between CDKN2A loss and stronger MDM2 dependency. This remains an association, not a causal or externally generalizable claim, and the remaining TP53, MTAP, and specificity follow-ups are important for interpreting the mechanism. H103 is rejected. The median IFN-gamma interaction for PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency had a small positive discovery estimate, +0.115 with interval +0.012 to +0.219, but independent validation was negative and null-compatible, -0.046 with interval -0.200 to +0.109. The independent interval excludes the discovery point estimate and provides no support for interaction. This is consistent with H92, where the top-quartile IFN interaction also failed to replicate cleanly. The robust conclusion is a main PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency, without reliable IFN context modification. Current supported dataset associations: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma and several context checks; TP53 wild-type status is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency broadly and in many contexts, including validated PIK3CA-mutant cells; and CDKN2A loss is newly supported as associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. These are scientifically meaningful magnitudes compared with the near-null genotype and receptor effects observed across the run. I registered 12 new dataset-level association comparisons focused on follow-up of the newly accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis, mechanistic specificity of that axis, and robustness/specificity checks for the strongest previously accepted axes. Signed interpretation follows the registered direction: for direction -1 main contrasts, a positive estimate indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group, meaning a more negative raw dependency score; for direction +1 main contrasts, a positive estimate indicates weaker dependency in the exposed group, meaning a less negative raw dependency score. Practical importance will require effects well above the recurring near-null scale of about 0.01-0.03 and near or above the stated 10 percent relative-difference threshold. The highest-priority proposals refine H132. First, I test the CDKN2A-loss association with MDM2 dependency in a context without TP53 loss or MTAP loss, to see whether the accepted effect is not merely an indirect consequence of p53-pathway or MTAP co-deletion. Second, I test MTAP loss within TP53 wild-type cells and test TP53 status within MTAP wild-type cells, which should help separate MTAP/9p21 deletion effects from TP53-pathway effects on MDM2. Third, I test the CDKN2A effect among high aneuploidy cells, because 9p21 deletions can co-occur with broad chromosomal instability. Fourth, I add cross-axis specificity checks: MTAP loss on STAT3 dependency and MTAP loss on USP7 dependency. For MTAP-USP7, direction +1 encodes the hypothesis that MTAP loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, which would be expected if MTAP/9p21 deletion marks TP53-loss or p53-pathway states. I also test MSI-high WRN dependency within high- and low-mutation-burden strata; this uses the previously tested mutation-burden interaction but asks for simple main effects in each burden group. Finally, I test accepted USP7/PTEN axes in selected contexts: TP53-wild-type USP7 dependency among MYC-amplified cells, PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency among MYC-amplified cells, and PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency among CDKN2A-loss and MTAP-loss cells. These are not causal claims and not claims about external generalizability. They are allocation-focused association tests designed to distinguish robust pathway-related effects from confounding, broad copy-number or MYC-state effects, or non-reproducible subgroup effects.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For the direction -1 MDM2 main contrasts, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative MDM2 dependency score, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency, than the comparator; for direction -1 interactions, a positive estimate means the CDKN2A-loss contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement; for the direction +1 USP7 contrast, a positive estimate would mean weaker USP7 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. H134 and H135 test the CDKN2A-loss effect separately in TP53 wild-type and TP53-loss cells. The signed estimates are +0.119 with interval +0.079 to +0.158 in TP53 wild-type cells and +0.111 with interval +0.035 to +0.186 in TP53-loss cells. Both are large relative to the recurring near-null dependency effects seen in this run and are above the practical 10% threshold on the MDM2 score scale, with intervals excluding null. I therefore accept H134 and H135 and close these specific subgroup tests. H136, the TP53-loss interaction, is -0.008 with interval -0.093 to +0.077; there is no evidence that TP53 loss modifies the CDKN2A effect, although the interval is not so narrow as to rule out a moderate interaction. I treat H136 as unsupported and close it because the stratified main effects are consistent. H137 tests MTAP loss overall on MDM2 dependency and H148 tests MTAP loss among TP53 wild-type cells. Their signed estimates are only +0.019 with interval -0.008 to +0.045 and +0.024 with interval -0.005 to +0.054, respectively. These positive trends are below the practical threshold I am applying on the MDM2 scale and their intervals include no effect; I therefore reject both as not scientifically meaningful evidence for MTAP loss alone. H149 tests TP53 wild-type versus loss among MTAP-intact cells and is essentially null, +0.003 with interval -0.025 to +0.031, supporting the conclusion that neither MTAP status nor TP53 status alone accounts for the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. H138 tests CDKN2A loss among MTAP-intact cells and is robust, +0.105 with interval +0.067 to +0.143; I accept and close it. H139 tests CDKN2A loss among MTAP-deleted cells and gives the largest point estimate, +0.165 with interval +0.081 to +0.249. The discovery interval is favorable, but the MTAP-deleted cells are a smaller and more co-deletion-enriched subset, and H140, the interaction for stronger effect in MTAP loss, is only +0.060 with interval -0.032 to +0.152 and does not establish reliable effect modification. Because this context is mechanistically important and potentially confounded by larger 9p21 deletions, I request independent validation of H139 and keep it unresolved pending that validation. H140 itself does not support an interaction conclusion; I reject and close it while noting that a moderate positive interaction remains possible but unproven. H141 tests CDKN2A-MDM2 in high-Cas9-quality screens and is robust, +0.116 with interval +0.070 to +0.161, so I accept and close this screen-quality check. H142 tests USP7 dependency in the opposite direction, expecting weaker USP7 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells, and is null: -0.002 with interval -0.043 to +0.038. H146 tests SMARCA2 dependency associated with CDKN2A loss and is also null, +0.009 with interval -0.032 to +0.050. Both reject and close; together they support specificity of the CDKN2A-MDM2 association rather than a broad dependency-state artifact. Overall, these results strengthen the interpretation that the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is robust across TP53 status, MTAP-intact status, MTAP-deleted status pending validation, and screen-quality selection, and that MTAP and TP53 main effects do not explain it. They remain dataset-level associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

The independent validation was directionally consistent but attenuated and inconclusive, +0.079 with interval -0.039 to +0.196. The validation point estimate is below the practical scale I have been using for robust MDM2 effects, the independent interval includes no effect, and the MTAP-deleted subset is smaller and enriched for 9p21 co-deletion patterns. I therefore do not accept the context-specific claim that MTAP-deleted cells amplify the CDKN2A-MDM2 association. I also do not reject it outright, because the validation point remains positive and overlaps the discovery estimate; the evidence is underpowered and confounded rather than clearly negative. The scientifically informative next step is to test whether MTAP loss adds association conditional on CDKN2A-loss status, and whether MTAP loss has an effect when CDKN2A is intact.

The main evidence-supported dataset-level associations are now: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency across the full sample and several contexts, including adenocarcinoma; TP53 wild-type status is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not the originally tested stronger-dependency direction; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency broadly, including in validated PIK3CA-mutant cells; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency overall and in validated and stratified contexts. record.narrative: No assessments are due and no validation capacity remains, so this stage registers focused follow-up comparisons and defers lower-priority untested active claims to keep the analysis allocation tight. All future estimates will be read exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator; for direction +1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a less negative score, i.e. weaker dependency. The highest-priority question is whether the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association is modified by MTAP deletion, TP53 status, broad chromosomal instability, or screen quality. I therefore registered conditional MTAP/CDKN2A/MDM2 tests in TP53 wild-type cells, a CDKN2A test within MTAP-deleted cells under high Cas9 activity, and a CDKN2A test in low-aneuploidy TP53 wild-type cells. I also added specificity checks asking whether MTAP loss itself carries a p53-like USP7-dependency signal and whether the accepted USP7, SMARCA2, NFE2L2, and STAT3 axes remain robust when MTAP-deleted status or TP53 wild-type status is imposed. I kept H64 and H147 active because they test USP7 TP53-status within MTAP-deleted cells and the clean triple context CDKN2A-loss TP53-WT MTAP-intact for MDM2, respectively. Other active no-evidence claims were deferred because they are lower-priority context expansions or near-duplicates of these more informative tests. These proposals remain dataset-level association queries, not causal claims and not claims about external generalizability.

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

expectation

record.narrative: No assessments are due and no independent validation capacity remains, so this analyze stage requests the twelve highest-priority currently active, untested comparisons. These are all discovery analyses, not new validations. I deliberately do not rerun already tested claims because previously tested comparisons reuse the same data and would not provide a new sample. Every returned estimate will be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator; for direction +1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive direction -1 estimate means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. The central scientific priority is to determine whether the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association is robust in mechanistically clean contexts and whether MTAP deletion modifies it. H161 asks whether MTAP loss adds MDM2 dependency among CDKN2A-loss TP53 wild-type cells. H162 asks whether MTAP loss has an MDM2 association among CDKN2A-intact TP53 wild-type cells. H147 tests CDKN2A loss in the cleaner TP53 wild-type, MTAP-intact context. H163 tests CDKN2A loss in high-Cas9-quality screens restricted to MTAP-deleted cells. H164 tests CDKN2A loss among low-aneuploidy TP53 wild-type cells to reduce broad copy-number instability confounding. If H161 is strong and H162 is null or much weaker, that would support a context-dependent MTAP interaction; if both are null or inconsistent, H139 should remain a nonvalidated subgroup fluctuation while the broader CDKN2A-MDM2 main effect remains accepted. I also request robustness and specificity checks around the other accepted axes. H165 tests whether the strong USP7 TP53 wild-type signal remains when MTAP is intact. H166 tests whether MTAP loss alone has any USP7-dependency association among TP53 wild-type cells. H167 and H168 test whether the accepted SMARCA2-SMARCA4 and NFE2L2-KEAP1 axes remain among MTAP-deleted cells. H169 tests whether the PTEN-loss STAT3 association remains among TP53 wild-type cells. H170 asks whether TP53 wild-type versus loss has an MDM2 association within MTAP-deleted cells. I will treat recurring near-null effects around 0.01 to 0.03 as practically unimportant on these dependency-score scales. Effects of about 0.10 or larger with intervals excluding null will be considered scientifically meaningful within this dataset. Intermediate positive estimates whose intervals include null will remain unresolved rather than accepted. These results, if obtained, remain dataset-level associations and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

Their signed estimates are only +0.019 with interval -0.008 to +0.045 and +0.024 with interval -0.005 to +0.054, respectively. These positive trends are below the practical threshold I am applying on the MDM2 scale and their intervals include no effect; I therefore reject both as not scientifically meaningful evidence for MTAP loss alone. H149 tests TP53 wild-type versus loss among MTAP-intact cells and is essentially null, +0.003 with interval -0.025 to +0.031, supporting the conclusion that neither MTAP status nor TP53 status alone accounts for the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. H138 tests CDKN2A loss among MTAP-intact cells and is robust, +0.105 with interval +0.067 to +0.143; I accept and close it. H139 tests CDKN2A loss among MTAP-deleted cells and gives the largest point estimate, +0.165 with interval +0.081 to +0.249. The discovery interval is favorable, but the MTAP-deleted cells are a smaller and more co-deletion-enriched subset, and H140, the interaction for stronger effect in MTAP loss, is only +0.060 with interval -0.032 to +0.152 and does not establish reliable effect modification. Because this context is mechanistically important and potentially confounded by larger 9p21 deletions, I request independent validation of H139 and keep it unresolved pending that validation. H140 itself does not support an interaction conclusion; I reject and close it while noting that a moderate positive interaction remains possible but unproven. H141 tests CDKN2A-MDM2 in high-Cas9-quality screens and is robust, +0.116 with interval +0.070 to +0.161, so I accept and close this screen-quality check. Both reject and close; together they support specificity of the CDKN2A-MDM2 association rather than a broad dependency-state artifact. For direction -1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator. For direction +1 main contrasts, a positive estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. For interactions, a positive direction -1 estimate means the named-subgroup comparison is stronger than the comparison in the subgroup complement.\n\nH114 is rejected and closed. The hypothesis was that EGFR amplification in KRAS-WT cells is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. The signed discovery estimate was negative, about -0.044 with interval -0.086 to -0.001, meaning the raw association was nominally opposite to the registered direction. The independent validation gave -0.022 with interval -0.084 to +0.040, null-compatible and close to the recurring near-null scale. Together, these provide no support for the EGFR-amplification STAT3-dependency claim in this dataset. The opposite direction claim H120 is likewise not supported by validation, because its independent interval also included null.\n\nH106 is accepted and closed. PTEN loss in PIK3CA-mutant cells was associated with stronger STAT3 dependency with discovery estimate +0.268, interval +0.127 to +0.409, and independent validation estimate +0.270, independent interval +0.068 to +0.472. The independent interval excludes null even with the stricter validation interval, the effect is large on the STAT3 dependency scale, and the point estimates are concordant. This supports a dataset-level PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association in PIK3CA-mutant cells. It does not imply causality or external generalizability. This accepted subgroup main effect remains compatible with rejected IFN-gamma and broader interaction tests, because the PTEN main effect appears in multiple contexts while context-specific interactions do not replicate reliably.\n\nH139 remains unresolved and active. CDKN2A loss among MTAP-deleted cells showed a strong discovery association with stronger MDM2 dependency, +0.165 with interval +0.081 to +0.249. The independent validation was directionally consistent but attenuated and inconclusive, +0.079 with interval -0.039 to +0.196. The validation point estimate is below the practical scale I have been using for robust MDM2 effects, the independent interval includes no effect, and the MTAP-deleted subset is smaller and enriched for 9p21 co-deletion patterns. I therefore do not accept the context-specific claim that MTAP-deleted cells amplify the CDKN2A-MDM2 association. I also do not reject it outright, because the validation point remains positive and overlaps the discovery estimate; the evidence is underpowered and confounded rather than clearly negative. The scientifically informative next step is to test whether MTAP loss adds association conditional on CDKN2A-loss status, and whether MTAP loss has an effect when CDKN2A is intact.\n\nThe main evidence-supported dataset-level associations are now: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency across the full sample and several contexts, including adenocarcinoma; TP53 wild-type status is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not the originally tested stronger-dependency direction; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency broadly, including in validated PIK3CA-mutant cells; and CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency overall and in validated and stratified contexts. These effects are much larger than the recurring 0.01 to 0.03 near-null genotype and receptor findings.\n\nImportant negative and specificity findings remain: KRAS mutation is not associated with KRAS dependency after validation; EGFR amplification is not robustly associated with EGFR or STAT3 dependency; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with ERBB2 or STAT3 dependency; MYC amplification is not associated with DHX9, KIF18A, or RPL11 dependency; PTEN loss is not associated with EGFR or ERBB2 dependency; KEAP1 loss is not associated with STAT3 dependency; TP53 wild-type status is not associated with STAT3 dependency; and most tested interactions, especially IFN-gamma interactions, fail validation. These negatives support pathway specificity rather than a broad dependency-state artifact.\n\nThe most informative next analyses are the two new conditional MTAP/CDKN2A tests: MTAP loss among CDKN2A-loss MDM2-dependency cells, and MTAP loss among CDKN2A-intact MDM2-dependency cells. If the first is robustly positive and the second is null or much smaller, MTAP co-deletion may amplify the CDKN2A-MDM2 association. If both are null or inconsistent, H139 should be treated as a non-validated subgroup fluctuation and the accepted conclusion should remain only the validated overall CDKN2A-MDM2 main effect. No validation requests remain, so subsequent resolution must come through discovery follow-up."}}

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered direction. For the direction -1 USP7, MDM2, SMARCA2, STAT3, and NFE2L2-related tests below, a positive main-effect estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator; for the direction +1 USP7 MTAP test, a positive estimate would mean weaker USP7 dependency in MTAP-deleted cells; for the direction +1 NFE2L2 KEAP1 test, a positive estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss, as previously established. H64 accepts the robustness of the USP7 axis within MTAP-deleted cells: TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss in MTAP-deleted cells has signed estimate +0.766, interval +0.719 to +0.813, a very large, precise association consistent with the validated overall USP7 TP53-wild-type effect. record.narrative:
Interpreting all estimates exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction: for direction -1, a positive estimate means exposed has stronger, more negative dependency than comparator; for direction +1, a positive estimate means exposed has weaker, less negative dependency; for direction -1 interactions, a positive estimate means the named-subgroup contrast is stronger than the complement contrast.

The due H132 validation is supportive and decisive for the dataset-level main claim. The discovery CDKN2A-loss association with MDM2 dependency was +0.117 with interval +0.082 to +0.152. Independent validation was +0.100 with stricter independent interval +0.049 to +0.151. The validation point is at the practical 0.10 dependency-score threshold and the independent interval excludes null. I therefore accept H132 and close the main CDKN2A-loss to stronger MDM2-dependency axis in this dataset.

The supported main axes are: SMARCA4 loss associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, about +0.78 to +0.80 after validation and robust across contexts; MSI-high associated with much stronger WRN dependency, about +0.79 to +0.81 after validation and robust; TP53 wild-type status associated with much stronger USP7 dependency, about +0.80 after validation; KEAP1 loss associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, about +0.80 after reversal to direction +1 and validation; PTEN loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, main about +0.27, validated +0.31, with robustness in multiple contexts and a validated PIK3CA-mutant subgroup effect about +0.27; CDKN2A loss associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, main now accepted with validated +0.10 and robustness in TP53 wild-type, MTAP-intact, high-Cas9, low-aneuploidy, TP53-loss, and adenocarcinoma contexts. These are dataset-level associations among measured variables in supplied lung-cancer-like cell-line models, not causal claims and not claims of external generalizability.

Important negative and specificity findings remain: KRAS mutation is not robustly associated with KRAS dependency; EGFR amplification is not robustly associated with EGFR or STAT3 dependency; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with ERBB2, TMED10, or STAT3 dependency; MYC amplification is not associated with DHX9, KIF18A, or RPL11 dependency; many receptor, p53-independent MDM2, USP7, and MYC-expression tests are near-null; IFN-gamma and SLFN11/other interaction hypotheses are not validated. I additionally reassess H92 as reject because its positive discovery IFN-gamma interaction did not replicate independently and the validation interval included no effect.

Unresolved uncertainty centers on MTAP-specific amplification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 axis. H139 remains closed unresolved: its independent validation was attenuated, and follow-up conditional tests did not establish MTAP deletion as a reliable modifier beyond the overall CDKN2A-loss effect. The accepted conclusion is the overall CDKN2A-MDM2 association, not MTAP co-deletion specificity. Other deferred subgroup claims remain lower-priority context extensions and do not alter the main set.

The most informative next analysis is technical-validity robustness: repeat the accepted main contrasts in low-Cas9 screens eligible cas9_activity_pct <=67.7 for SMARCA2, WRN, USP7, MDM2, STAT3, and NFE2L2. This directly tests whether the large accepted dependency signals are screen-quality-dependent. If effects remain similar and exclude null, the dataset-level associations are more credible as biology-like patterns; if they attenuate, claims should be restricted to adequate Cas9 activity. I also registered one orthogonal context test of CDKN2A-MDM2 under high 8q24 copy number and one new broad STAT3/MSI-high exploration, but low-Cas9 robustness is the highest priority because no new validation capacity remains.

Iteration 12/25, stage explore, attempt 1.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

All estimates will be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered direction: for these direction -1 hypotheses, a positive signed estimate supports the hypothesis and indicates that the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than the comparator; a negative signed estimate would support the opposite or a null-to-reverse pattern. A practical benchmark remains about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units with intervals excluding null for scientific importance; intervals including null will not be accepted. The first proposal tests whether the near-null main BRAF mutation signal becomes detectable in a mechanistically cleaner KRAS-wild-type context. The alternative is that BRAF mutation status remains not meaningfully associated with BRAF dependency or that the estimate is too small to be important. The second proposal tests the accepted CDKN2A-loss MDM2-dependency association within screen_batch batch_a, completing an important batch robustness check because the other large accepted axes have already been examined in batch_a but the CDKN2A-MDM2 axis has not. The third and fourth proposals test whether the largest accepted axis robustness signals persist under higher chromosomal instability, defined by aneuploidy_score at or above the upper-quantile threshold 0.483. These genomic-instability tests ask whether the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect and TP53-wild-type USP7 effect are confounded by broad copy-number instability or are robust across high-aneuploidy cells. record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no new independent validation requests remain. I activate H150 and request the 12 highest-value discovery analyses from the active pool. The priority is technical-validity robustness for the six accepted large/intermediate dependency axes under low Cas9 activity (cas9_activity_pct <= 67.7): H171 SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, H172 MSI-high/WRN, H173 TP53 wild-type/USP7, H174 CDKN2A loss/MDM2, H175 PTEN loss/STAT3, and H176 KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2. H176 is direction +1, so a positive signed estimate again means weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss, consistent with the accepted reversal. For direction -1 hypotheses, positive signed estimates mean exposed has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than comparator. These estimates must not be multiplied by direction again.

I also request robustness of accepted axes in important contexts: H150 tests CDKN2A loss/MDM2 dependency in high aneuploidy, completing copy-number instability robustness for the CDKN2A-MDM2 axis; H180 tests CDKN2A loss/MDM2 in batch_a; H181 tests SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 in high aneuploidy; and H182 tests TP53 wild-type/USP7 in high aneuploidy. If these remain near prior magnitudes with intervals excluding null, the dataset-level associations are less likely to be driven by low Cas9 quality, batch, or high aneuploidy confounding. If they attenuate or include null, acceptance should be restricted to adequate Cas9 or relevant contexts.

H179 asks whether BRAF-mutant cells show stronger BRAF dependency in the mechanistically cleaner KRAS-wild-type context; the prior overall BRAF-mutation contrast was near null. H178 is a broad exploratory STAT3 test, asking whether MSI-high cells have stronger STAT3 dependency than MSI-stable cells. Practical interpretation will use about 0.10 dependency-score units with interval excluding null for meaningful acceptance; very large effects around 0.8 are clearly important within this dataset, whereas near-null effects around 0.01-0.03 are not. Positive estimates with intervals including null will remain unresolved unless supported by context and size. These remain associations among measured variables, not causal or external generalizability claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 hypotheses, a positive estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group, because the raw contrast is negative, i.e. more negative for exposed than comparator. For H176, direction +1 and positive estimate supports weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss, consistent with the earlier accepted reversal. The low-Cas9 robustness panel H171-H176 supports robustness of the main accepted axes under cas9_activity_pct <=67.7. H171 SMARCA4-loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in low-Cas9 screens: +0.754, CI +0.712 to +0.797, n=[85,345]. H172 MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency: +0.798, CI +0.732 to +0.864, n=[27,403]. H173 TP53 wild-type status associated with stronger USP7 dependency: +0.795, CI +0.751 to +0.838, n=[340,90]. H175 PTEN-loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.372, CI +0.268 to +0.476, n=[73,357]. H176 KEAP1 loss associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: +0.799, CI +0.751 to +0.847, n=[84,346]. These effects are large or very large relative to the dependency-score scale, intervals exclude zero, and they are broadly consistent with the previously accepted main axes. I therefore accept H171, H172, H173, H175, and H176 and close them as completed low-Cas9 robustness checks. This reduces concern that the accepted SMARCA2, WRN, USP7, STAT3, and NFE2L2 associations depend on high-Cas9 screens. H174 tests CDKN2A loss and MDM2 dependency in low-Cas9 screens: +0.109, CI +0.046 to +0.172, n=[89,341]. This is not attenuated relative to the main CDKN2A-MDM2 axis and excludes null, but it is near the practical 0.10 threshold and imprecise. I accept it as context-supporting, while noting that the magnitude is less certain than the large axes. The accepted main CDKN2A-MDM2 association remains the primary claim. Context checks for accepted axes are also supportive. H150 tests CDKN2A loss and MDM2 dependency in high-aneuploidy cells: +0.138, CI +0.064 to +0.212, n=[105,396]. H180 tests the same association in screen_batch batch_a: +0.119, CI +0.052 to +0.187, n=[93,426]. H181 tests SMARCA4 loss and SMARCA2 dependency in high-aneuploidy cells: +0.759, CI +0.721 to +0.798, n=[102,399]. H182 tests TP53 wild-type and USP7 dependency in high-aneuploidy cells: +0.791, CI +0.751 to +0.831, n=[391,110]. These intervals exclude null and magnitudes remain compatible with the accepted main axes, so I accept H150, H180, H181, and H182 and close them. They argue against the hypothesis that the MDM2, SMARCA2, or USP7 associations are primarily driven by high aneuploidy or batch_a composition, although they do not establish causality or external generalizability. The two negative tests are clear. H178 asks whether MSI-high cells have stronger STAT3 dependency overall: +0.016, CI -0.027 to +0.059. The point estimate is near null and the interval includes no effect, so I reject the claim of a meaningful MSI-high STAT3 association in this dataset. H179 tests BRAF-mutant versus BRAF-wild-type dependency within KRAS-wild-type cells: -0.019, CI -0.051 to +0.013. The signed estimate is slightly opposite to the registered direction, tiny, and includes null. I reject the claim of a meaningful BRAF-mutation effect on BRAF dependency in the KRAS-wild-type context. No independent validation is requested because no new validation requests remain. Overall, these results strengthen the evidence that the major accepted axes are dataset-level technical and genomic context robust: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, TP53 wild-type/USP7, KEAP1 loss/weaker NFE2L2, PTEN loss/STAT3, and CDKN2A loss/MDM2, with the CDKN2A-MDM2 magnitude closer to the practical threshold and more uncertain than the very large axes.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
Synthesis: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction; for direction -1, positive means the exposed group has a more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency score than the comparator. The H139 response deadline concerns whether CDKN2A loss has a meaningfully stronger association with MDM2 dependency specifically in MTAP-loss-positive lines. The discovery estimate was +0.165 (95% CI +0.081 to +0.249), but the independent validation estimate was +0.079 with the stricter independent interval -0.039 to +0.196. The validation point estimate is below the 0.10 dependency-score-unit practical threshold and its interval includes no effect, so it does not confirm a meaningful MTAP-specific amplification. I therefore reject H139 as an established dataset-level association. This is not a proof of zero, but the independent evidence does not support MTAP co-deletion as a reliable modifier beyond the main CDKN2A-MDM2 effect.

Final supported findings: The supplied dataset supports several dataset-level association axes. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, with main effect about +0.78 and validated about +0.80; it is robust in adenocarcinoma, low-Cas9 screens, high-aneuploidy cells, MTAP-loss-positive eligibility, and other accepted context checks. MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, main about +0.79 and validated about +0.81; it is robust across lineage subtype, BRCA2-loss-negative, adherent culture, low-Cas9 screens, batch_a, and adequate-Cas9 eligibility. TP53 wild-type status is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency, about +0.80 after validation; it is robust in CDKN2A-loss and CDKN2A-intact subgroups, adherent culture, batch_a, low-Cas9 screens, MTAP-loss-negative eligibility, and high-aneuploidy cells. KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, represented by the accepted reversal H17 with validated estimate about +0.80, and robust in low-Cas9, batch_a, STK11-loss-positive, MTAP-loss-positive, and adequacy-eligibility contexts. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, main about +0.27 and validated about +0.31; it is robust across batch, Cas9 eligibility, culture, lineage, low/intermediate IFN-gamma signature, SLFN11-high, PIK3CA-positive, TP53 wild-type, and low-Cas9 contexts. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, main about +0.117 and validated +0.100 with independent interval excluding null; it is robust in TP53 wild-type and TP53-loss subgroups, MTAP-loss-negative eligibility, high-Cas9 and low-Cas9 screens, batch_a, high-aneuploidy, low-aneuploidy with TP53 wild-type, and several other accepted context checks.

Negative or unsupported findings: Many nominally plausible gene-state to dependency associations are near-null or unsupported. BRAF V600E is not meaningfully associated with BRAF dependency, including in KRAS-wild-type eligibility. KRAS mutation is not robustly associated with KRAS dependency; the validation estimate is essentially null. EGFR amplification is not associated with EGFR dependency in overall, adenocarcinoma, KRAS-wild-type, or STK11-wild-type contexts, and EGFR amplification in KRAS-wild-type cells did not support stronger STAT3 dependency after validation. ERBB2 amplification is not associated with ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency, and not associated with STAT3 dependency. MYC amplification is not associated with DHX9, KIF18A, or RPL11 dependency overall or in MYC-expression-high eligibility. Research markers D, E, and F show no meaningful associations with the tested dependencies. Many interaction hypotheses fail to show modification: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effects are not modified by ARID1A loss, lineage subtype, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, or STK11 loss; TP53 wild-type USP7 effects are not modified by CDKN2A loss, KEAP1 loss, MTAP-loss-positive status, aneuploidy, or lineage in accepted interaction tests; PTEN-loss STAT3 effects are not supported as modified by PIK3CA mutation, SLFN11 expression, lineage subtype, TP53 loss, STK11 loss, high IFN-gamma, or ifn-gamma above zero; CDKN2A-loss MDM2 effects are not meaningfully modified by TP53 loss or MTAP loss as an interaction; and MSI-high WRN effects are not meaningfully modified by lineage subtype or high mutation burden in tested interaction analyses. The MTAP-specific amplification of CDKN2A-MDM2 is not confirmed and is now rejected as an established association.

Unresolved uncertainty: Deferred or unresolved subgroup/context claims do not materially alter the main supported set. Biological mechanisms, causal direction, therapeutic relevance, and external generalizability remain unestablished. The MTAP co-deletion question is at most uncertain and likely unsupported as a modifier: discovery suggested amplification but independent validation was attenuated and imprecise, and the interaction test did not establish modification. Technical robustness within this dataset is much stronger than it was earlier because the major axes persist under low Cas9 activity, different batches, aneuploidy strata, culture type, and lineage subsets, but this only reduces some dataset-specific confounding concerns; it does not prove causality.

Most informative next analysis: No independent validation requests remain. If further external work is possible, the highest-value step is independent replication of the accepted axes in an external cohort, especially the intermediate CDKN2A-MDM2 and PTEN-STAT3 effects, and a larger pre-specified test of whether MTAP co-deletion modifies CDKN2A-MDM2. Within the supplied dataset, the next most useful analysis would be a summary of conditional dependence of accepted axes on screen-quality and genomic-instability covariates using the existing Welch comparisons, but current evidence already supports robustness and additional low-power subgroup tests are unlikely to add much.

Study instructions:

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no new independent-validation requests remain. I therefore register six targeted refinements of the already supported dependency axes, rather than reopening low-prior nominal gene-state tests. All returned estimates will be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will not be re-signed. For direction -1 mean_difference hypotheses, a positive signed estimate supports the hypothesis and means the exposed group has a more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency score than the comparator. For the NFE2L2 direction +1 hypothesis, a positive signed estimate supports the accepted reversal pattern: KEAP1-loss lines are less dependent on NFE2L2, i.e. have a more positive or less negative dependency score than KEAP1-intact lines.

Each proposal restricts an accepted axis to higher screen quality using screen_nnmd >= -7.353, the median and therefore the upper half of the screen_nnmd distribution. screen_nnmd is a continuous screen-quality metric that has not previously been used as an eligibility filter, so these are useful complementary technical robustness checks after Cas9 activity, batch, culture, lineage, and aneuploidy strata. If these estimates remain near the accepted main-effect magnitudes and 95% intervals exclude null, the dataset-level associations are less likely to be driven by low screen quality. If they attenuate or become null, acceptance should be restricted to higher-quality screen contexts, although such attenuation would not prove the original association is causal or false; it would only indicate context dependence within this supplied dataset.

The six axes are: SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency; TP53 wild-type versus stronger USP7 dependency, implemented as exposure 0 versus comparator 1; KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, implemented with direction +1; PTEN loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency; and CDKN2A loss versus stronger MDM2 dependency. The CDKN2A-MDM2 association is intermediate in magnitude, around 0.10 to 0.12 dependency-score units, so this screen-quality restriction is especially informative. If the interval excludes null in this context, it further supports retaining the accepted MDM2 association; if it includes null, the accepted association should be interpreted cautiously and confined to the main and validated evidence. For all proposals, intervals that include null or point estimates far below the practical importance benchmark will not be accepted. These remain associations among measured variables in the supplied dataset, not claims about causality or external generalizability.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
