Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;

with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

No assessments are due and no independent-validation requests remain. I will request 12 discovery analyses focused on the remaining high-value robustness checks for the accepted dataset-level dependency axes. All estimates will be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will not be multiplied by direction again. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger dependency in the exposed group than comparator; for H186 direction +1, a positive estimate supports weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines, consistent with the accepted reversal.

The first six are the active screen-quality refinements: H183 SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, H184 MSI-high/WRN, H185 TP53-wild-type/USP7, H186 KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, H187 PTEN-loss/STAT3, and H188 CDKN2A-loss/MDM2, each restricted to screen_nnmd >= -7.353. These test whether the accepted axes persist in the upper half of the screen-quality distribution after Cas9 activity, batch, culture, lineage, aneuploidy, and MTAP-context checks. Persistence with intervals excluding null would reduce concern about screen-quality confounding; attenuation would motivate restricting acceptance to higher-quality screens but would not by itself prove causality or disprove the main association.

The remaining six prioritize scientifically informative contexts where accepted axes have not yet been directly tested. H152 and H153 test MSI-high/WRN dependency in mutation-burden high versus low eligibility. This is important because MSI status and mutation burden are correlated; persistence in the low-burden stratum would support an MSI association not simply explained by high mutation burden, whereas a null low-burden estimate would indicate burden context dependence. H27 tests TP53-wild-type/USP7 dependency in adenocarcinoma, completing major lineage-subtype robustness for the USP7 axis. H154 tests TP53-wild-type/USP7 dependency in MYC-amplified lines, complementing the accepted MYC-negative robustness check. H177 tests CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 dependency in the upper copy_number_8q24 stratum, adding locus-specific copy-number instability robustness beyond whole-genome aneuploidy checks. H31 tests KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency in TP53-wild-type lines, a common co-mutation context; the direction is +1, so a positive estimate again means weaker NFE2L2 dependency with KEAP1 loss.

For acceptance at appraisal, I will use the practical importance threshold of about 0.10 dependency-score units for intermediate effects, with interval excluding null; effects near 0.7-0.8 on the dependency scale are very large within this dataset. Near-null effects or effects below practical importance, even if precise, will not be treated as meaningful. These analyses test associations among measured variables in the supplied dataset only; they do not establish causality or external generalizability.

For direction -1 mean differences, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative, stronger dependency score than the comparator. For H186 and H31, direction +1 and a positive estimate supports the accepted reversal pattern: KEAP1-loss lines are weaker NFE2L2 dependencies than KEAP1-intact lines. The screen-quality panel H183-H187 strongly supports the main accepted axes in the upper half of screen_nnmd: SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss +0.761 [0.734,0.788]; WRN/MSI-high +0.791 [0.747,0.836]; USP7/TP53-wild-type +0.797 [0.767,0.826]; NFE2L2 reversal/KEAP1-loss +0.793 [0.764,0.821]; STAT3/PTEN-loss +0.324 [0.247,0.400]. These are large effects, close to the previously accepted or validated main effects, with intervals excluding zero. I accept them as robustness evidence and close them as completed technical-quality checks. H188 MDM2/CDKN2A-loss is +0.108 [0.060,0.157], just above the practical 0.10 dependency-score-unit benchmark but imprecise, with lower confidence bound below that benchmark. I accept it only as context-supporting evidence for the already accepted and validated main CDKN2A-MDM2 association, not as a strong independent claim, and close it to avoid overinterpreting a marginal context test. H152 and H153 test MSI-high/WRN within high and low mutation-burden strata, with large estimates +0.772 [0.733,0.811] and +0.798 [0.747,0.849]. This argues the MSI/WRN dependency association is not simply a proxy for high mutation burden in this dataset, although median-split strata are imperfect and residual genomic confounding cannot be excluded. I accept and close them. H27 and H154 show the TP53-wild-type/USP7 axis remains very large in adenocarcinoma, +0.799 [0.776,0.823], and MYC-amplified lines, +0.803 [0.754,0.852]; accept and close. Multiplicity is relevant because many low-prior context checks have been tested. I did not treat borderline context effects as independent discoveries; the very large accepted axes are unlikely to be explained by multiplicity or these screen-quality/genomic strata. record.narrative: No new independent-validation requests remain, assessments_due is empty, and the H139 MTAP-specific CDKN2A-MDM2 response was already resolved by attenuated independent validation. I therefore assess no new discovery evidence, request no further independent validation, and do not register additional low-value supplied-dataset subgroup comparisons. All reported estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction: for direction -1 mean differences, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative, stronger dependency score; for the NFE2L2 direction +1 reversal, a positive estimate means KEAP1-loss lines are less negative, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependencies than KEAP1-intact lines. The final scientific report is as follows. Supported dataset-level associations: First, SMARCA4 loss is robustly associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The accepted main association H12 is +0.784 on the signed dependency scale with 95% CI +0.765 to +0.803 and independent validation R13 +0.800 CI +0.768 to +0.832. This is far above the 10% relative practical threshold and is robust across adenocarcinoma H25, ARID1A-intact H60, adequate and low Cas9 screens H58/H171, batch_a H59, higher screen quality H183, high aneuploidy H181, MTAP-loss-positive eligibility H167, and other accepted context checks. It is not modified by ARID1A loss H23, lineage subtype H26, TP53 loss H37, KEAP1 loss H110, or STK11 loss H118 in the tested comparisons. Second, MSI-high is robustly associated with stronger WRN dependency. H16 is +0.790 CI +0.760 to +0.819 with validation R39 +0.807 CI +0.759 to +0.855. Adenocarcinoma-specific H21 is also supported and validated. The association persists in both high and low mutation-burden eligibility, H152 +0.772 CI +0.733 to +0.811 and H153 +0.798 CI +0.747 to +0.849, reducing concern that MSI-high WRN dependency is merely a proxy for high mutation burden within this dataset. It is also robust in BRCA2-loss-negative H76, adherent culture H57, batch_a H56, low Cas9 screens H172, and higher screen quality H184. Tested lineage and mutation-burden interaction hypotheses did not establish modification. Third, TP53 wild-type status is robustly associated with stronger USP7 dependency relative to TP53 loss, implemented as exposure 0 versus comparator 1. H15 is +0.802 CI +0.782 to +0.822 with validation R53 +0.799 CI +0.769 to +0.828. Robust contexts include CDKN2A-intact H28, CDKN2A-loss H41, adenocarcinoma H27, MYC-amplified H154, higher screen quality H185, low Cas9 screens H173, MTAP-loss-negative eligibility H165, higher aneuploidy H182, and adequate screen quality metrics. Tested interaction hypotheses by CDKN2A loss H29, KEAP1 loss H40, aneuploidy H83, STK11 loss H111, and others did not establish effect modification. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, accepted as the direction +1 reversal H17/H8 complement: +0.796 CI +0.776 to +0.816 with validation R26 +0.801 CI +0.772 to +0.829. This reversal is robust in adenocarcinoma H20, TP53-wild-type lines H31, STK11-loss-positive lines H63, MTAP-loss-positive eligibility H168, low Cas9 screens H176, batch_a H62, and higher screen quality H186. The interpretation is that KEAP1-loss lines have less negative NFE2L2 scores, not stronger NFE2L2 dependency. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H81 is +0.267 CI +0.215 to +0.319 and independent validation R66 +0.310 CI +0.231 to +0.388. This exceeds the practical threshold and is robust in batch_a H84, adequate and low Cas9 eligibility H85/H175, adherent culture H86, adenocarcinoma H87, PIK3CA-positive subgroup H106 validated, PIK3CA-negative H90, lower/intermediate IFN-gamma signature H102, SLFN11-high H104, TP53-wild-type H169, and higher screen quality H187. However, tested interaction hypotheses did not establish modification by PIK3CA mutation H88, high IFN-gamma H92, IFN-gamma above zero H103, SLFN11-high H105, lineage subtype H108, TP53 loss H109, or STK11 loss H112; the validated high IFN-gamma and IFN-gamma above zero interaction estimates were not confirmed. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H132 is +0.117 CI +0.082 to +0.152 with independent validation R120 +0.100 CI +0.049 to +0.151. This is an intermediate effect but remains above the practical importance benchmark in the main and validated comparisons and is robust in TP53-wild-type H134, TP53-loss H135, MTAP-loss-negative eligibility H138/H147, adequate and low Cas9 screens H141/H174, batch_a H180, higher and lower aneuploidy contexts H150/H164, and higher screen quality H188. However, near-threshold context checks such as H188 +0.108 CI +0.060 to +0.157 and high copy_number_8q24 H177 +0.103 CI +0.039 to +0.167 should be treated only as supportive context, not as strong independent claims. Interaction hypotheses by TP53 loss H136 and MTAP loss H140 did not establish meaningful modification, and the MTAP-specific mean MDM2 effect H139 was not confirmed after independent validation. Negative or unsupported findings: The supplied dataset does not support several canonical matched-gene dependency hypotheses. BRAF V600E is not meaningfully associated with BRAF dependency overall H1 or in KRAS-wild-type eligibility H125/H179. KRAS mutation is not robustly associated with KRAS dependency; H6 discovery was weak and validation was essentially null R80. record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no independent-validation requests remain. I therefore register twelve scientifically motivated comparisons, combining focused follow-up of accepted dependency axes with a small set of untested but pathway-relevant predictor-outcome hypotheses. All returned estimates will be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction and will not be re-signed. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative, stronger dependency score than the comparator. For the accepted USP7 axis proposals using exposed=0 and comparator=1, a positive estimate means TP53 wild-type lines have stronger USP7 dependency than TP53-loss lines. For direction -1 interactions, a positive signed interaction means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative in the subgroup than in the complement, i.e. a stronger effect in that subgroup.

The first panel tests biologically plausible new main associations. NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK signaling and may create or strengthen pathway-specific dependencies, so I test NF1 loss against BRAF dependency. PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, which increases translational and ribosome-biogenesis programs; this motivates testing PTEN loss against RPL11 dependency. RB1 loss affects the p53-MDM2 and cell-cycle landscape, so I test RB1 loss against MDM2 and USP7 dependency. MSI-high lines have characteristic genome instability, replication stress, and DNA-repair vulnerabilities, motivating a new test of MSI-high against KIF18A dependency. TP53 loss alters transcriptional stress handling and cell-fate control, motivating POLR2A dependency testing, though the expected direction is uncertain.

The second panel follows accepted axes with targeted refinements rather than low-prior nominal screening. PTEN loss is accepted as associated with stronger STAT3 dependency; I test whether this effect is context-dependent in high EMT and high hypoxia strata, because mesenchymal and hypoxic states can alter inflammatory-signaling dependencies. CDKN2A loss is accepted as associated with stronger MDM2 dependency; I test modification by RB1 loss and by high 8q24 copy number, because these capture p53/RB pathway context and locus-specific copy-number instability beyond whole-genome aneuploidy checks. The accepted TP53 wild-type-USP7 axis is tested as modified by RB1 loss. The accepted SMARCA4 loss-SMARCA2 synthetic-lethality-like association is tested for modification by MTAP loss, a co-deletion context that could matter biologically even if the main MTAP effect on CDKN2A-MDM2 did not replicate.

These comparisons use common markers or quartile/upper-half continuous splits where practical to preserve adequate Welch cells. They remain associations among measured variables in the supplied dataset only; confirmatory or null results will not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. For intermediate effects, especially any new main effects or interaction modifiers, I will require both an interval that excludes null and a magnitude that is scientifically meaningful relative to the dependency-score scale, rather than relying on nominal p-value significance alone.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

status (accept/reject/unresolved),

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction; I did not re-multiply by direction. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate supports stronger, more negative dependency in the exposed group, whereas a negative signed estimate indicates the opposite. For interactions, a positive signed interaction indicates a stronger exposed-minus-comparator effect in the named subgroup than in the complement. H189, H190, H191, H193, and H194 are all small and interval-crossing: NF1-loss/BRAF, PTEN-loss/RPL11, RB1-loss/MDM2, MSI-high/KIF18A, and TP53-loss/POLR2A show no scientifically meaningful association in the supplied dataset, so I reject them and close them. H192 is the most notable exception: RB1 loss versus USP7 gives a signed estimate -0.059 with interval -0.112 to -0.006, excluding zero in the signed scale, but this is opposite to the H192 direction -1 claim. In raw terms, the point estimate suggests RB1-loss cells have less negative USP7 scores, i.e., weaker USP7 dependency, not stronger. The interval is still uncertain and includes lower-magnitude values, and this was a low-prior comparison in a large screening set with no independent-validation capacity remaining. I therefore reject the original H192 direction and register a reversal proposal linked to H192 for any future confirmation; I do not accept it as an established claim from this single discovery evidence. H195, high EMT modifying PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, is nominally positive +0.141 with interval +0.011 to +0.271. The point exceeds a practical interaction benchmark, but the lower bound is close to negligible, and the PTEN-STAT3 modification family has largely failed to replicate or establish modifiers. Given multiplicity and uncertainty, I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than accepting it as robust context-specific evidence. H196 through H200 are null or very small interaction tests: high hypoxia does not modify PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency; RB1 loss and high 8q24 copy number do not establish meaningful modification of CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency; RB1 loss does not establish modification of the TP53-wild-type USP7 axis in the interaction test; and MTAP loss does not modify SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency. I reject them as evidence for meaningful effect modification and close them. No new accepted axis is added. The previously supported dataset-level axes remain SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, TP53-wild-type/USP7, KEAP1-loss reversed weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN-loss/STAT3, and CDKN2A-loss/MDM2. These remain associations among measured variables in this supplied dataset only, not causal, therapeutic, or external-generalizability claims.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

I therefore allocate the twelve discovery tests to the highest-value combination of pre-specified technical robustness and current biologically motivated hypotheses. I request H202-H207, the six accepted predictor-dependency axes under high screen_roc_auc eligibility, to test whether the SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-high-WRN, TP53-wild-type-USP7, KEAP1-loss-NFE2L2, PTEN-loss-STAT3, and CDKN2A-loss-MDM2 associations persist in better-quality screens. These cover the most plausible non-signature proposals from the explore step while avoiding a larger multiplicity burden from arbitrary research-signature interaction tests. H208-H213 high-ploidy robustness remain active for possible future context testing. All returned estimates will be interpreted exactly as already signed to the registered direction. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction; I did not re-multiply by direction. H202-H206 provide a high screen_roc_auc eligibility robustness panel for the accepted predictor-dependency axes. The intervals are large, precise, and exclude the null: SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency, TP53 wild type versus loss versus stronger USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency. I accept these context-specific results as dataset associations. They are not independent validation because validation request capacity is exhausted, but they strengthen within-dataset technical robustness. H207, the high screen_roc_auc CDKN2A-loss versus MDM2 dependency test, has a positive point estimate of about +0.071 but a CI that crosses null, from -0.006 to +0.149. This is too uncertain to support the high-quality-screen context claim. I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than rejecting the overall accepted CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association, because the subset is smaller and the interval is close to zero. I registered one follow-up proposal testing CDKN2A-loss versus MDM2 dependency in the upper half of screen_roc_auc to clarify whether this is power loss or a genuine attenuation in higher-quality screens. H214, H217, H218, and H219 are small, interval-crossing main-effect tests for MYC amplification versus MDM2, APC mutation versus STAT3, KEAP1 loss versus WRN, and PTEN loss versus WRN. These were biologically plausible but exploratory; I reject them as meaningful dataset associations. H220 and H221 test MYC amplification as a modifier of accepted CDKN2A-loss MDM2 and PTEN-loss STAT3 axes. Both intervals are wide and cross null with small point interactions, so I reject them as evidence of meaningful modification. I also reassessed H201, the low-prior reversal suggesting RB1 loss associated with weaker USP7 dependency. R173 is nominally positive on the signed scale, +0.059 with lower bound +0.006, but the magnitude is small, the interval is close to negligible, it arose in a large screening context with many nominal tests, and no independent confirmation capacity remains. I reject it rather than leave an unsupported reversal open. No new validation can be requested.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

No new validation results or validation response deadlines are present at this synthesis. The independent-validation request budget is exhausted, and assessments_due is empty, so no new accept/reject decisions can or should be made from validation evidence. I also did not change any claim status on the basis of this stage alone. The next analyses are already queued in the active investigation set: H226 clarifies the unresolved CDKN2A-loss MDM2 axis under upper-half screen ROC-AUC, and H208-H213 test the six accepted axes under high-ploidy eligibility. 

Scientific synthesis of the supplied dataset: the evidence strongly supports six predictor-dependency associations. (1) SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H12/R9 +0.784, 95% CI +0.765 to +0.803, independently validated by R13 +0.800 CI +0.768 to +0.832, and robust across adenocarcinoma, Cas9 strata, culture, batch, aneuploidy, MTAP-loss-positive, and high screen ROC-AUC contexts (H202/R182). (2) MSI-high is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency: H16/R12 +0.790 CI +0.760 to +0.819, validated by R39 +0.807 CI +0.759 to +0.855, and robust in adenocarcinoma, high/low mutation-burden, BRCA2-loss-negative, Cas9, batch, and high screen ROC-AUC contexts (H203/R183). (3) TP53 wild-type status is associated with markedly stronger USP7 dependency relative to TP53 loss: H15/R11 +0.802 CI +0.782 to +0.822, validated by R53 +0.799 CI +0.769 to +0.828, and robust across CDKN2A states, lineage, MYC, MTAP, aneuploidy, Cas9, and screen-quality contexts (H204/R184). (4) KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H17/R6 signed +0.796 CI +0.776 to +0.816, validated by R26 +0.801 CI +0.772 to +0.829, and robust across lineage, TP53, STK11, MTAP, batch, Cas9, and screen-quality contexts (H205/R185). (5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H81/R63 +0.267 CI +0.215 to +0.319, validated by R66 +0.310 CI +0.231 to +0.388, and robust across many biological and technical contexts including high screen ROC-AUC (H206/R186). (6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H132/R119 +0.117 CI +0.082 to +0.152, validated by R120 +0.100 CI +0.049 to +0.151, and robust across TP53/MTAP/Cas9/batch/aneuploidy contexts; however, the narrow very-high screen ROC-AUC subset H207/R187 remains unresolved (+0.071 CI -0.006 to +0.149), which motivated H226. 

These effects are large and internally consistent, and several have independent validation or strong technical robustness. The task relevance threshold of 10% relative difference maps roughly to small absolute dependency-score shifts near the observed mean dependency levels, but the accepted axes include both very large effects and the intermediate PTEN-STAT3 and CDKN2A-MDM2 axes, whose intervals exclude the null and have magnitudes well above the small-effect zone. Nevertheless, these remain associations among measured variables in this supplied dataset, not evidence of causality, synthetic lethality, therapeutic vulnerability, or external generalizability. 

Important negative findings include lack of support for many canonical matched-gene dependency hypotheses: BRAF V600E versus BRAF dependency, KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency (weak discovery followed by near-null validation), EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency across major contexts, ERBB2 amplification versus ERBB2/TMED10 dependency, MYC amplification versus DHX9/KIF18A/RPL11/MDM2 dependency, RB1 loss versus MDM2 dependency, NF1 loss versus BRAF dependency, PTEN loss versus WRN or RPL11 dependency, KEAP1 loss versus WRN dependency, APC mutation versus STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss versus POLR2A dependency, and MSI-high versus KIF18A dependency. The constructed research markers D/E/F show no meaningful associations. Many effect-modifier tests are negative, including ARID1A modification of SMARCA4-SMARCA2, lineage or mutation-burden modification of MSI-WRN, TP53/KEAP1/STK11/MTAP modification of accepted USP7/SMARCA2/NFE2L2/STAT3 axes, PIK3CA or SLFN11 modification of PTEN-STAT3, and TP53/MTAP modification of CDKN2A-MDM2. The previously low-prior RB1-loss USP7 reversal H201 is now closed as rejected rather than accepted, because R173 is small in magnitude, close to null at the lower bound, and arose in a low-prior screen without confirmation capacity. 

Unresolved areas are narrow and mainly involve possible context modification or underpowered high-quality-screen subsets: H207/R187 for CDKN2A-loss MDM2 under very high screen ROC-AUC, H195/R176 for high EMT modification of PTEN-loss STAT3, and H208-H213 for high-ploidy context. These are not accepted claims. The most informative next analysis is to complete the pre-specified H226 CDKN2A-MDM2 upper-half screen ROC-AUC main-effect test and the H208-H213 high-ploidy panel. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. record.narrative:
All estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction; no additional sign multiplication was applied. The high-ploidy eligibility panel H208-H213 shows that all six previously accepted predictor-dependency axes remain strongly associated in this genomic-context subset. H208 SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency is +0.769, 95% CI +0.730 to +0.807. H209 MSI-high versus WRN dependency is +0.790, CI +0.729 to +0.850. H210 TP53 wild-type versus TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency is +0.797, CI +0.758 to +0.836. H211 KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency is +0.808, CI +0.766 to +0.849. H212 PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency is +0.228, CI +0.127 to +0.329. H213 CDKN2A loss versus MDM2 dependency is +0.106, CI +0.036 to +0.175. All intervals exclude the null in the hypothesized direction. The first four are very large on the dependency-score scale; the last two are intermediate but comparable to their already accepted and validated main effects, and are practically meaningful relative to the typical dependency-score scale. I accept these as dataset-specific context robustness results, not causal or externally generalizable claims. Some exposed cell counts are modest, especially MSI-high in high ploidy, so exact uncertainty is wider there, but the intervals remain decisive.

H226 resolves the broader upper-half screen-quality context for CDKN2A loss and MDM2 dependency: signed effect +0.132, CI +0.081 to +0.184. This supports the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association in a broader high-ROC-AUC population and reduces concern from the underpowered very-high-quality subset H207. It should not be read as confirmation of exact very-high ROC-AUC subgroup specificity; H207 remains a narrow unresolved subset.

H227 and H228 provide direct EMT-stratum contrasts for PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency. The PTEN-loss association is positive and CI-excluding in high EMT (+0.378, CI +0.261 to +0.495) and in low EMT (+0.237, CI +0.179 to +0.295). This indicates the PTEN-STAT3 axis is present across EMT states. The high-EMT point estimate is larger, and the earlier interaction H195 was nominally positive, but because that interaction has a close lower bound and was tested amid many modifiers, I treat the direct strata as the safer evidence and do not need to promote the interaction to a strong accepted modifier at this stage.

H230 and H231 test two accepted intermediate axes in KRAS-mutant lines. PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency is +0.249, CI +0.139 to +0.358, and CDKN2A loss versus MDM2 dependency is +0.168, CI +0.092 to +0.243. Both support the accepted axes within KRAS-mutant context. This is scientifically useful because KRAS mutation could have rewire signaling or cell-cycle dependencies, but the data remain compatible with persistence of these associations. These are still associations among measured variables in the supplied dataset.

H235 tests ARID1A loss versus WRN dependency as a replication-stress/DNA-repair hypothesis. The signed effect is only +0.022 with CI -0.009 to +0.053. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent-validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore step registers twelve new discovery comparisons that test two complementary ideas. First, I register direct biomarker and proliferation predictors for outcomes not fully explored by the accepted axes. The STAT3 hypotheses are that cell-intrinsic interferon-gamma signaling, high AXL expression, and hypoxia increase STAT3 dependency (raw more negative scores), direction -1. The mechanistic rationale is that AXL and hypoxia can activate STAT3-associated stress and survival programs, while interferon signaling can alter STAT pathway activity. Plausible alternatives are that these biomarkers mark inflammation, resistance, or lineage state without changing STAT3 essentiality, producing null or opposite effects. The WRN hypotheses are that higher aneuploidy or higher SLFN11 expression increases WRN dependency, direction -1, through replication stress and DNA-damage-associated replication stress. The null hypothesis is that WRN dependency remains primarily tied to MSI-high biology and is not strongly modified by these broader replication-stress markers. The proliferation-core hypotheses are that fast-growing lines have stronger dependency on POLR2A, RPL11, and DHX9, direction -1, because rapid proliferation should require more transcription, translation, and RNA processing. A plausible alternative is that growth rate is confounded by screen quality or does not translate into measurable dependency differences. Second, I register follow-up context tests for accepted axes. CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency should persist among fast-growing lines if the p53 pathway association is not merely a low-proliferation artifact; attenuation would suggest proliferation context matters. PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency should persist among high-AXL lines, testing whether the accepted axis survives in a resistance/EMT-like state. SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency and KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency are tested in lower-ploidy lines to complement the accepted high-ploidy robustness panel. I expect these large accepted axes to persist, but the lower-ploidy test remains useful because chromatin remodeling and NRF2 pathway effects could depend on aneuploidy or genome instability. All proposed contrasts are in the supplied lung-lineage dataset and will be interpreted as associations among measured variables, not causal, synthetic-lethal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims. Direction -1 means the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is negative, i.e., stronger dependency in the exposed group, except for the KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 comparison, where direction +1 means the accepted raw positive exposed-minus-comparator difference indicates weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. For continuous exposure claims, the registered exposed value is the threshold used to define the high-expression or high-score group, following the controller's prior continuous-threshold convention.

The mechanistic rationale is that AXL and hypoxia can activate STAT3-associated stress and survival programs, while interferon signaling can alter STAT pathway activity. Plausible alternatives are that these biomarkers mark inflammation, resistance, or lineage state without changing STAT3 essentiality, producing null or opposite effects. The WRN hypotheses are that higher aneuploidy or higher SLFN11 expression increases WRN dependency, direction -1, through replication stress and DNA-damage-associated replication stress. PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency should persist among high-AXL lines, testing whether the accepted axis survives in a resistance/EMT-like state. SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency and KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency are tested in lower-ploidy lines to complement the accepted high-ploidy robustness panel. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent-validation capacity is exhausted, so I allocate the twelve available discovery analyses to unresolved context tests and the newly registered direct-predictor hypotheses. H229 resolves whether the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association attenuates in the lower-half screen_roc_auc population, complementing the accepted broad main effect, the broader upper-half quality test H226, and the unresolved very-high-quality subset H207. H232-H234 complete the KRAS-mutant context panel for the large USP7, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2 axes; this tests whether oncogenic KRAS mutation rewires these dependencies. H236-H238 test MYC expression above the median log2 TPM threshold against DHX9, POLR2A, and RPL11 dependency, distinguishing transcriptional/translation dependence on MYC expression from the repeatedly null MYC-amplification hypotheses. H239-H241 test direct high IFN-gamma, high AXL, and high hypoxia predictors of STAT3 dependency, while H242-H243 test direct high aneuploidy and high SLFN11 predictors of WRN dependency. These direct tests are more informative than further replication of already accepted genotype-anchored axes because they can reveal independent biomarker correlates or close those mechanistic hypotheses. I defer H244-H246 because growth-rate effects overlap the MYC-expression core-dependency tests and may be confounded by screen quality or proliferation state; I defer H247-H248 because CDKN2A-MDM2 and PTEN-STAT3 already survived KRAS-mutant, EMT-stratum, and screen-quality tests; and I defer H249-H250 because the high-ploidy context panel already supports all six accepted axes, making lower-ploidy robustness less urgent than direct-predictor discovery. All returned estimates are interpreted exactly as already signed to the registered direction: positive signed values support the hypothesized raw more negative dependency in the exposed/high-threshold group. H229 and H232-H234 are expected to produce large or intermediate intervals if accepted axes persist, and should be judged against the 10 percent relative-difference threshold and cell-count uncertainty. The direct predictor hypotheses have lower prior effect-size expectation and will be accepted only if the signed CI excludes the null and the point estimate is scientifically meaningful on the dependency-score scale, not merely nominally significant.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All estimates were interpreted exactly as signed to the registered direction; no additional sign multiplication was applied. H229/R206 tests CDKN2A loss versus MDM2 dependency in the lower-half screen_roc_auc population. The signed estimate is +0.103 with 95% CI +0.056 to +0.150. Because the hypothesis direction is -1, this corresponds to a raw lower MDM2 dependency score by about 0.10 in CDKN2A-loss lines relative to CDKN2A-intact lines, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. The interval excludes the null and the magnitude is comparable to the accepted main effect and upper-half screen-quality tests. This supports persistence of the CDKN2A-MDM2 association even when screen ROC quality is lower. I accept H229 as a dataset-specific quality-context result and close it. This also reduces concern from the underpowered very-high-quality subset H207; I therefore close H207 as a low-priority unresolved precision question rather than leaving it active.

H232/R207, H233/R208, and H234/R209 test the large TP53-WT-USP7, SMARCA4-loss-SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss-NFE2L2 axes within KRAS-mutant lines. Signed estimates are +0.783 (CI +0.741 to +0.826), +0.774 (CI +0.733 to +0.814), and +0.805 (CI +0.767 to +0.843), respectively. All are very large on the dependency-score scale and intervals decisively exclude the null in the expected direction. H234 is direction +1, so the positive signed result again means KEAP1-loss lines have raw weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. These are context-specific confirmations in an important oncogenic signaling subset, not independent external validation. They remain in-dataset associations and may be partially confounded by KRAS co-mutation patterns, but the effects are so large that the primary conclusion is persistence of the axes rather than artifact. I accept H232-H234 and close them.

H236-H243 are different: R210-R217 are invalid diagnostic results with null estimates and insufficient cell counts. The issue is not a failed biological hypothesis but an analysis-coding mismatch. These claims used continuous thresholds as exposed/comparator values, but the Welch cell-count diagnostic appears to evaluate exact-value exposure/comparator cells, giving exposed or comparator groups with zero or fewer than 20 observations. Therefore no scientific estimate exists. I keep them unresolved because they are not evidence against the biological hypotheses, but close them as not testable in the current exact-cell mean_difference framework. The same coding issue applies to H244-H246, direct continuous-threshold main effects for growth rate, so I close those as well. H247-H250 remain useful because they use thresholds as eligibility/subgroup conditions and binary exposures, not as exact-value main-effect contrasts.

I also close H222-H225, arbitrary research-signature modifier interactions, because these constructed assays have no assigned gene/pathway and the prior probability of a scientifically meaningful effect modifier is low relative to the multiplicity already incurred. This is not a rejection based on effect direction; it is a resource allocation and inference-control decision. The accepted evidence base is already broad, and continuing arbitrary-signature interaction tests would primarily add multiplicity risk.

Overall, the newly delivered valid results strengthen the accepted context robustness panel: the accepted axes persist in KRAS-mutant context and in a lower screen-quality stratum. The invalid continuous direct-predictor tests should not be interpreted as null evidence. No validation is requested because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. Next, I register lower-ploidy context refinements for USP7, STAT3, MDM2, and WRN to complement the active lower-ploidy SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 tests. These are more informative than additional continuous-threshold direct effects that cannot be tested under the current cell-count convention.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.
