record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent-validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore step registers new discovery comparisons using designs that avoid the exact-value continuous-threshold cell-count failure seen earlier. The main active scientific priority remains the lower-ploidy robustness panel H249-H254, high-AXL PTEN/STAT3 H248, and fast-growth CDKN2A-MDM2 H247; these are left unchanged. New proposals add two complementary classes of valid tests. First, I register direct binary PI3K-pathway predictors of RTK and RAS-pathway dependency outcomes: PIK3CA mutation versus EGFR, ERBB2, and KRAS dependency among KRAS-wildtype lines. The falsifiable hypothesis is that downstream PI3K/AKT pathway activation bypasses upstream RTK or RAS dependency, giving raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency scores that are less negative and therefore signed positive under direction +1. The alternative is that PIK3CA mutation does not reduce upstream dependency or is too weakly related in these lines to matter. I also register PIK3CA mutation versus MDM2 dependency among TP53-wildtype lines, expecting PI3K/AKT signaling to increase MDM2 pathway dependence and therefore produce raw more negative MDM2 dependency, signed positive under direction -1. Second, I register accepted-axis context tests in faster-growing lines using growth-rate eligibility rather than continuous main-effect contrasts. SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-wildtype USP7 dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, and MSI-high WRN dependency should persist if these associations are not artifacts of slow-growing or low-proliferation lines. Attenuation would identify proliferation as an important context limitation. The HER2/EGFR cross-amplification tests examine whether one amplified RTK increases dependency on the other, a biologically meaningful heterodimerization/co-dependency hypothesis; the null is that amplification of one receptor creates bypass independence rather than co-dependency. RB1-loss versus STAT3 dependency is a focused new predictor test for an underexplored STAT3 correlate, based on the idea that Rb loss and E2F/transcriptional dysregulation may alter STAT pathway dependence; null or opposite effects remain plausible. For all claims, returned estimates are to be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered direction and judged against CI exclusion, magnitude on the dependency-score scale, and the 10 percent relative-difference relevance threshold. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations among measured lung-lineage CRISPR dependencies, not causal, synthetic-lethal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

The main active scientific priority remains the lower-ploidy robustness panel H249-H254, high-AXL PTEN/STAT3 H248, and fast-growth CDKN2A-MDM2 H247; these are left unchanged. New proposals add two complementary classes of valid tests. First, I register direct binary PI3K-pathway predictors of RTK and RAS-pathway dependency outcomes: PIK3CA mutation versus EGFR, ERBB2, and KRAS dependency among KRAS-wildtype lines. The falsifiable hypothesis is that downstream PI3K/AKT pathway activation bypasses upstream RTK or RAS dependency, giving raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency scores that are less negative and therefore signed positive under direction +1. The alternative is that PIK3CA mutation does not reduce upstream dependency or is too weakly related in these lines to matter. I also register PIK3CA mutation versus MDM2 dependency among TP53-wildtype lines, expecting PI3K/AKT signaling to increase MDM2 pathway dependence and therefore produce raw more negative MDM2 dependency, signed positive under direction -1. Second, I register accepted-axis context tests in faster-growing lines using growth-rate eligibility rather than continuous main-effect contrasts. SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-wildtype USP7 dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, and MSI-high WRN dependency should persist if these associations are not artifacts of slow-growing or low-proliferation lines. Attenuation would identify proliferation as an important context limitation. The HER2/EGFR cross-amplification tests examine whether one amplified RTK increases dependency on the other, a biologically meaningful heterodimerization/co-dependency hypothesis; the null is that amplification of one receptor creates bypass independence rather than co-dependency. RB1-loss versus STAT3 dependency is a focused new predictor test for an underexplored STAT3 correlate, based on the idea that Rb loss and E2F/transcriptional dysregulation may alter STAT pathway dependence; null or opposite effects remain plausible. For all claims, returned estimates are to be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered direction and judged against CI exclusion, magnitude on the dependency-score scale, and the 10 percent relative-difference relevance threshold. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations among measured lung-lineage CRISPR dependencies, not causal, synthetic-lethal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.","analyze":"No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze step allocates the twelve available discovery analyses to the highest-value unresolved tests that use valid binary-exposure designs with eligibility or subgroup constraints rather than exact-value continuous main-effect contrasts. These tests ask whether the large or intermediate accepted effects persist in a genomically more euploid context, complementing the accepted high-ploidy robustness panel. H248 tests the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 axis within high-AXL eligibility, a resistance-like expression context that was flagged as particularly informative because it uses a valid binary exposure with an expression-threshold eligibility. H247 tests the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 axis in faster-growing lines, complementing screen-quality, mutation-context, and ploidy robustness tests. H255-H258 test direct PI3K-pathway hypotheses: PIK3CA mutation as a downstream bypass marker for EGFR, ERBB2, and KRAS dependency among KRAS-wild-type lines under direction +1, and PIK3CA mutation as a potential enhancer of MDM2 dependency among TP53-wild-type lines under direction -1. I defer H259-H263 because those accepted-axis fast-growth tests overlap the same robustness logic already partly addressed by H247 and would add less new information than the lower-ploidy panel and PIK3CA direct-predictor tests. I also defer H264-H266 because the new receptor cross-amplification and RB1-STAT3 hypotheses are useful but lower priority than completing the accepted-axis robustness panel and PI3K pathway test set. All new results will be interpreted exactly as signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency score is more negative, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed score is less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. No causal, therapeutic, synthetic-lethal, or external-generalization claim is made from these in-dataset associations.","appraise":"All estimates were interpreted exactly as signed to the registered direction; no additional sign multiplication was applied. H229/R206 tests CDKN2A loss versus MDM2 dependency in the lower-half screen_roc_auc population. The signed estimate is +0.103 with 95% CI +0.056 to +0.150. Because the hypothesis direction is -1, this corresponds to a raw lower MDM2 dependency score by about 0.10 in CDKN2A-loss lines relative to CDKN2A-intact lines, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. The interval excludes the null and the magnitude is comparable to the accepted main effect and upper-half screen-quality tests. This supports persistence of the CDKN2A-MDM2 association even when screen ROC quality is lower. I accept H229 as a dataset-specific quality-context result and close it. This also reduces concern from the underpowered very-high-quality subset H207; I therefore close H207 as a low-priority unresolved precision question rather than leaving it active.\n\nH232/R207, H233/R208, and H234/R209 test the large TP53-WT-USP7, SMARCA4-loss-SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss-NFE2L2 axes within KRAS-mutant lines. Signed estimates are +0.783 (CI +0.741 to +0.826), +0.774 (CI +0.733 to +0.814), and +0.805 (CI +0.767 to +0.843), respectively. All are very large on the dependency-score scale and intervals decisively exclude the null in the expected direction. H234 is direction +1, so the positive signed result again means KEAP1-loss lines have raw weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. These are context-specific confirmations in an important oncogenic signaling subset, not independent external validation. They remain in-dataset associations and may be partially confounded by KRAS co-mutation patterns, but the effects are so large that the primary conclusion is persistence of the axes rather than artifact. I accept H232-H234 and close them.\n\nH236-H243 are different: R210-R217 are invalid diagnostic results with null estimates and insufficient cell counts. The issue is not a failed biological hypothesis but an analysis-coding mismatch. These claims used continuous thresholds as exposed/comparator values, but the Welch cell-count diagnostic appears to evaluate exact-value exposure/comparator cells, giving exposed or comparator groups with zero or fewer than 20 observations. Therefore no scientific estimate exists. I keep them unresolved because they are not evidence against the biological hypotheses, but close them as not testable in the current exact-cell mean_difference framework. The same coding issue applies to H244-H246, direct continuous-threshold main effects for growth rate, so I close those as well. H247-H250 remain useful because they use thresholds as eligibility/subgroup conditions and binary exposures, not as exact-value main-effect contrasts.\n\nI also close H222-H225, arbitrary research-signature modifier interactions, because these constructed assays have no assigned gene/pathway and the prior probability of a scientifically meaningful effect modifier is low relative to the multiplicity already incurred. This is not a rejection based on effect direction; it is a resource allocation and inference-control decision. The accepted evidence base is already broad, and continuing arbitrary-signature interaction tests would primarily add multiplicity risk.\n\nOverall, the newly delivered valid results strengthen the accepted context robustness panel: the accepted axes persist in KRAS-mutant context and in a lower screen-quality stratum. The invalid continuous direct-predictor tests should not be interpreted as null evidence. No validation is requested because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. Next, I register lower-ploidy context refinements for USP7, STAT3, MDM2, and WRN to complement the active lower-ploidy SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 tests. These are more informative than additional continuous-threshold direct effects that cannot be tested under the current cell-count convention.","synthesize":"No new validation results and no response deadlines were delivered. assessments_due is empty and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so I make no claim status changes. All estimates below are interpreted exactly as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction; no additional sign multiplication is applied. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, i.e. the exposed group has a raw more negative dependency score and therefore stronger dependency. For the KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 claims with direction +1, a positive signed estimate means KEAP1-loss lines have raw weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. All conclusions are associations among measured variables in this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR screen dataset, not causal, synthetic-lethal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims. Supported findings: the evidence base now strongly supports six dataset-specific genotype-context axes. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H12/R9 +0.784 95% CI +0.765 to +0.803, independently replicated by R13 +0.800 CI +0.768 to +0.832. This pattern is robust in adenocarcinoma context H25/R19 +0.777 CI +0.755 to +0.799, in ARID1A-intact lines H60/R49 +0.777 CI +0.756 to +0.798, across screen-quality and proliferation contexts, and in KRAS-mutant lines H233/R208 +0.774 CI +0.733 to +0.814. Second, MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, H16/R12 +0.790 CI +0.760 to +0.819, replicated by R39 +0.807 CI +0.759 to +0.855, with adenocarcinoma context H21/R17 +0.784 CI +0.748 to +0.820 and validation R40 +0.813 CI +0.754 to +0.872. Third, TP53 wild type, coded as TP53_loss exposure 0 versus comparator 1, is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss, H15/R11 +0.802 CI +0.782 to +0.822, replicated by R53 +0.799 CI +0.769 to +0.828, and robust across many contexts including KRAS-mutant lines H232/R207 +0.783 CI +0.741 to +0.826. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H17/R6 +0.796 CI +0.776 to +0.816, replicated by R26 +0.801 CI +0.772 to +0.829, with KRAS-mutant context H234/R209 +0.805 CI +0.767 to +0.843. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, H81/R63 +0.267 CI +0.215 to +0.319, replicated by R66 +0.310 CI +0.231 to +0.388, and observed in many strata including KRAS-mutant lines H230/R203 +0.249 CI +0.139 to +0.358, high-EMT stratum H227/R201 +0.378 CI +0.261 to +0.495, and low-EMT stratum H228/R202 +0.237 CI +0.179 to +0.295. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, H132/R119 +0.117 CI +0.082 to +0.152, replicated by R120 +0.100 CI +0.049 to +0.151, with KRAS-mutant context H231/R204 +0.168 CI +0.092 to +0.243, broad upper-half screen-quality context H226/R200 +0.132 CI +0.081 to +0.184, and lower-half screen-quality context H229/R206 +0.103 CI +0.056 to +0.150. The four very large axes have interval widths and point magnitudes far beyond null on the dependency-score scale; the PTEN-STAT3 and CDKN2A-MDM2 effects are intermediate but CI-excluding, replicated, and meet the task relevance threshold as dataset-specific associations. Context robustness: the same axes persist across many biologically and technical subsets, including high ploidy H208-H213, KRAS mutation H232-H234, screen-quality strata H226/H229/H202-H207, EMT strata H227/H228, and lineage subtype or culture contexts where tested. Negative findings: many intuitive matched-gene dependencies are absent or too small. BRAF V600E does not support stronger BRAF dependency H1/R1. KRAS mutation does not support stronger KRAS dependency H6/R4, with near-null validation R80. EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency H3/R2 or in adenocarcinoma, KRAS-WT, or combined contexts H18/R14, H33/R24, H128/R118. ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency H4/R3, H14/R25, H127/R117. MYC amplification does not support stronger DHX9, KIF18A, RPL11, or MDM2 dependency H2/R108, H5/R109, H11/R110, H214/R188. RB1 loss does not support stronger MDM2 dependency H191/R172. NF1 loss does not support stronger BRAF dependency H189/R170. PTEN loss does not support stronger WRN or RPL11 dependency H219/R191 and H190/R171. KEAP1 loss does not support stronger WRN dependency H218/R190. MSI-high does not support stronger KIF18A dependency H193/R174. ARID1A loss does not support stronger WRN dependency H235/R205. Constructed research markers D/E/F show no meaningful associations H45/R35, H46/R36, H47/R37, H48/R38. Several effect-modifier hypotheses are negative or failed independent validation, including IFN-gamma modification of PTEN-STAT3 H92/R75 plus validation R79 and H103/R82 plus validation R93, and MTAP modification of CDKN2A-MDM2 H139/R126 plus validation R133. record.narrative:
All newly delivered estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction; no additional sign multiplication is applied. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency score is more negative, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed group. For the KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 direction +1 claim, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency.  

The accepted-axis robustness panel is strengthened. H247/R218 tests CDKN2A loss versus MDM2 dependency among faster-growing lines and gives +0.090 (95% CI +0.038 to +0.143). Because direction is -1, this means CDKN2A-loss lines have raw stronger MDM2 dependency than CDKN2A-intact lines in the fast-growth eligibility. The interval excludes the null, the point estimate is comparable to the accepted main effect H132/R119 (+0.117) and lower-quality screen-quality strata, and the lower bound is above the approximate 10% relative-difference relevance benchmark on the dependency-score scale. I accept H247 as a dataset-specific fast-growth context result and close it. Residual concerns remain that fast-growth eligibility is selected on a measured proliferation proxy and may be correlated with culture, screen, or genomic context, but the effect is sufficiently large and consistent to support persistence of the CDKN2A-MDM2 association in this subset.  

H248/R219 tests PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency within high-AXL expression eligibility and gives +0.286 (CI +0.177 to +0.395). This is direction -1, so it indicates raw stronger STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss lines even in the AXL-high context. The magnitude is similar to or larger than the main PTEN-STAT3 effect and validation, the interval excludes the null comfortably, and it exceeds the relative-size relevance threshold. I accept H248 and close it. This supports, rather than undermines, the accepted PTEN-STAT3 axis in a resistance-like expression context.  

H249-H254/R220-R225 complete the lower-ploidy robustness panel. All signed estimates are large and in the expected direction: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 +0.792 (CI +0.752 to +0.833); KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 +0.776 (CI +0.736 to +0.817); TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 +0.801 (CI +0.762 to +0.841); PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 +0.193 (CI +0.094 to +0.292); CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 +0.117 (CI +0.042 to +0.192); MSI-high stronger WRN +0.788 (CI +0.737 to +0.838). Every interval excludes the null in the registered direction, and the magnitudes are well above the 10% relevance benchmark. I accept all six lower-ploidy context claims and close them. These are not independent external validations; they are in-dataset context tests. However, given the effect sizes for SMARCA2, USP7, NFE2L2, and WRN, the dominant scientific interpretation is persistence of the axes under lower-ploidy eligibility. For PTEN-STAT3 and CDKN2A-MDM2, the lower-ploidy estimates are somewhat smaller than some high-ploidy or global estimates but remain positive, statistically distinct from null, and above the relevance threshold.  

The direct PI3K-pathway hypotheses are not supported. H255/R226, H256/R227, and H257/R228 test whether PIK3CA mutation in KRAS-wildtype lines is associated with weaker EGFR, ERBB2, or KRAS dependency under direction +1. Signed estimates are +0.002 (CI -0.023 to +0.027), +0.011 (CI -0.014 to +0.036), and -0.001 (CI -0.026 to +0.025), respectively. All intervals include the null and point estimates are negligible on the dependency-score scale; they do not provide evidence for a clinically meaningful relative difference. H258/R229 tests whether PIK3CA mutation among TP53-wildtype lines is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency under direction -1 and gives +0.001 (CI -0.029 to +0.031), also null. I reject H255-H258 and close them as not supported. Competing explanations include imperfect binary coding of PI3K-pathway activation, heterogeneity of KRAS-wildtype or TP53-wildtype subsets, dependence of RTK/RAS dependency on upstream pathway features not captured by PIK3CA mutation, and the possibility that PIK3CA mutation is too sparse or biologically weak to shift these dependency scores in this dataset. These rejections are dataset-specific negative associations, not claims about lack of biological bypass mechanisms in general.  

Overall, this batch strengthens the accepted robustness evidence for the six main dataset-specific axes and fails to support new PIK3CA-based direct-predictor hypotheses. No validation request is made because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted.

record.narrative: No assessments were due and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so no new validation was requested. I assessed all validation evidence present in the ledger against the registered hypothesis direction, interpreting returned estimates exactly as already signed and not applying any additional sign transformation. The central conclusion is that the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR screen dataset contains several large, reproducible, dataset-specific genotype dependency associations, while many direct matched-gene dependency hypotheses and effect-modifier hypotheses are absent or too uncertain to support. Six main axes are well supported. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H12/R9 plus validation R13, with broad context robustness including adenocarcinoma H25/R19, ARID1A-intact lines H60/R49, fast and slow screen-quality contexts, high and low ploidy, KRAS-mutant lines H233/R208, MTAP-loss lines H167/R142, and lower-ploidy lines H249/R220. Second, MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, H16/R12 plus validation R39, replicated in adenocarcinoma H21/R17 plus validation R40, and robust across many screen and genomic contexts including H55, H56, H57, H76, H152, H153, H172, H184, H203, H209, H254. Third, TP53 wild-type status, coded as exposure 0 versus comparator 1 for TP53 loss, is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss, H15/R11 plus validation R53, with robustness across many contexts including KRAS-mutant lines H232/R207, adenocarcinoma H27/R166, and lower ploidy H251/R222. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H17/R6 plus validation R26, robust in adenocarcinoma H20/R16, TP53-intact lines H31/R169, KRAS-mutant lines H234/R209, and lower-ploidy lines H250/R221. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, H81/R63 plus validation R66, and robust across many contexts including lower ploidy H252/R223, high EMT H227/R201, low EMT H228/R202, high AXL eligibility H248/R219, TP53-intact H169/R144, PIK3CA-mutant subgroup H106/R85 plus validation R107, and KRAS-mutant lines H230/R203. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, H132/R119 plus validation R120, robust across many contexts including fast-growth eligibility H247/R218, KRAS-mutant lines H231/R204, and broad screen-quality halves H226/R200 and H229/R206. These are dataset-specific associations, not causal, synthetic-lethal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims. Negative findings are also substantial. Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

evidence assessment.

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H12/R9 plus validation R13, with broad context robustness including adenocarcinoma H25/R19, ARID1A-intact lines H60/R49, fast and slow screen-quality contexts, high and low ploidy, KRAS-mutant lines H233/R208, MTAP-loss lines H167/R142, and lower-ploidy lines H249/R220. Second, MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, H16/R12 plus validation R39, replicated in adenocarcinoma H21/R17 plus validation R40, and robust across many screen and genomic contexts including H55, H56, H57, H76, H152, H153, H172, H184, H203, H209, H254. Third, TP53 wild-type status, coded as exposure 0 versus comparator 1 for TP53 loss, is associated with much stronger USP7 dependency than TP53 loss, H15/R11 plus validation R53, with robustness across many contexts including KRAS-mutant lines H232/R207, adenocarcinoma H27/R166, and lower ploidy H251/R222. record.narrative: All newly delivered estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. The fast-growth robustness panel is very strong. H259/R230 gives a signed effect of +0.759 for SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency in faster-growing lines, with a tight interval that excludes null and a magnitude far above any plausible 10% relevance threshold. H260/R231 gives +0.807 for TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 dependency under the same growth-rate eligibility. H261/R232 gives +0.814 for KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, consistent with the accepted direction. H262/R233 gives +0.288 for PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, similar to the accepted main and validated effect. H263/R234 gives +0.776 for MSI-high stronger WRN dependency. These effects are large relative to the scale of the corresponding dependency scores, have stable cell counts, and are inconsistent with mere chance. I therefore accept H259-H263 as dataset-specific fast-growth context support for the six main axes and close them. Residual concerns remain that fast-growth eligibility is a measured, correlated phenotype and these are not external validations, but the effect sizes are too large for those concerns to overturn the in-dataset conclusion. The receptor co-dependency tests are null. H264/R235 estimates +0.0004 for ERBB2-amplification associated EGFR dependency among EGFR-amplification-negative lines, with a null interval and negligible magnitude. H265/R236 estimates -0.0117, opposite the registered direction and imprecise. I reject H264 and H265. These are dataset-specific lack-of-association results, not proof that RTK dependency cannot be context dependent elsewhere. H266/R237 tests RB1 loss as a direct STAT3 predictor and gives +0.0386, with a 95% interval of +0.0032 to +0.0740. This supports a small positive association with stronger STAT3 dependency in RB1-loss lines, but the lower bound is close to null and the effect is much smaller than the dominant PTEN-loss STAT3 axis. Given multiplicity, the modest magnitude, and the possibility that RB1 loss partially tracks with other pathway lesions such as PTEN loss, I leave H266 unresolved and active, and register a PTEN-intact restricted direct test and an RB1-by-PTEN interaction test to assess whether the signal is independent of the dominant PTEN-loss STAT3 association. The interaction panel does not support meaningful context modification except for a borderline serum effect. H267/R238, an attenuating CDKN2A-loss-by-fast-growth interaction for MDM2 dependency, estimates -0.045 with a null interval; no evidence of attenuation is established, and the accepted fast-growth main effect remains. H268/R239, a PTEN-loss-by-fast-growth interaction for STAT3 dependency, is near zero and imprecise, again supporting robustness of the parent axis rather than fast-growth modification. H270/R241, a SMARCA4-loss-by-serum-rich interaction for SMARCA2 dependency, has a small positive interval crossing zero, so no evidence for serum-dependent attenuation or enhancement. I reject these interaction claims as directional claims because their intervals include zero and the parent main effects are already accepted. H269/R240, KEAP1-loss-by-serum-rich interaction for NFE2L2 dependency, is statistically positive but small, +0.043 with lower bound near null. It may indicate a slight enhancement of the KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 association in serum-rich culture, but the magnitude is minor relative to the very large main effect and the interval is not robust enough to accept as a clinically or mechanistically important modifier. I leave it unresolved but closed, given that the main KEAP1-NFE2L2 association is already robust and further effort is better spent on the unresolved RB1-STAT3 follow-up. No validation is requested because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. These conclusions are limited to the supplied dataset; they are not claims about causality, synthetic lethality, therapeutic vulnerability, or generalization.

Context robustness now includes fast growth for all six and many screen-quality, ploidy, subtype, and co-genotype panels.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore step registers four high-value discovery effect-modification claims that can complement the already active H259-H266 without repeating the invalid exact-threshold continuous main-effect coding used earlier. Each proposal uses a binary genotype exposure and a continuous measured context threshold as an interaction subgroup, which should satisfy cell-count requirements better than numeric exposure contrasts. The interaction direction is deliberately chosen to match the accepted parent axis for that outcome. Therefore, after sign conversion, a positive signed estimate means the exposure-comparator dependency difference is enhanced in the subgroup relative to its complement, whereas a negative signed estimate means attenuation. An interval excluding zero would provide evidence for context modification; an interval centered near zero would support robustness of the parent axis in that context. The CDKN2A-loss MDM2 fast-growth interaction asks whether the accepted CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 dependency persists with the same magnitude in faster-growing lines. The main-effect fast-growth association H247 is already supported, but this interaction tests whether proliferation state changes the magnitude; no raw interaction is expected if the association is intrinsic, while attenuation would make the fast-growth association context-dependent. The PTEN-loss STAT3 fast-growth interaction is analogous for the PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 axis, where growth-factor-rich or proliferation-related biology could plausibly alter STAT3 dependency if the association is partly culture-state dependent. The serum-rich KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 interaction tests whether serum concentration modifies the strong KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency association, with attenuation identifying a possible dependence on oxidative-stress or medium context. The serum-rich SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 interaction tests whether the very strong SMARCA4-loss synthetic-lethal-like association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency is invariant under serum-rich culture, with attenuation as the falsification. These are dataset-specific context robustness tests, not causal, therapeutic, or generalizable claims. If analysis capacity is limited, active H259-H266 remain scientifically prior because they test persistence of the six accepted axes in fast growth, receptor co-dependency, and RB1-loss STAT3; the four new interactions are registered to use remaining high-quality slots or refine context interpretation after those active tests.","analyze":"No assessments are due, and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze step allocates all available discovery-analysis slots to the currently active unresolved claims. H259-H263 test whether the six major accepted dataset-specific axes persist among faster-growing lines: SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, and MSI-high stronger WRN dependency. H264 and H265 test receptor cross-dependency logic: whether ERBB2 amplification is associated with EGFR dependency among EGFR-amplification-negative lines, and whether EGFR amplification is associated with ERBB2 dependency among ERBB2-amplification-negative lines. H266 tests RB1 loss as a direct predictor of STAT3 dependency, a useful direct predictor not covered by the accepted PTEN-STAT3 robustness panel. H267-H270 test context modification: fast-growth interactions for CDKN2A-loss MDM2 and PTEN-loss STAT3, and serum-rich interactions for KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 and SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2. All returned estimates must be interpreted exactly as already signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, positive signed values indicate raw stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, positive signed values indicate raw weaker dependency in the exposed group; for interactions, signed estimates indicate enhancement or attenuation of the subgroup contrast relative to the complement. If any comparison returns insufficient-cell_n, it will be appraised as an analysis-coding or precision limitation rather than biological null.","appraise":"All newly delivered estimates are interpreted exactly as signed to the registered hypothesis direction. The fast-growth robustness panel is very strong. H259/R230 gives a signed effect of +0.759 for SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency in faster-growing lines, with a tight interval that excludes null and a magnitude far above any plausible 10% relevance threshold. H260/R231 gives +0.807 for TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 dependency under the same growth-rate eligibility. H261/R232 gives +0.814 for KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, consistent with the accepted direction. H262/R233 gives +0.288 for PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, similar to the accepted main and validated effect. H263/R234 gives +0.776 for MSI-high stronger WRN dependency. These effects are large relative to the scale of the corresponding dependency scores, have stable cell counts, and are inconsistent with mere chance. I therefore accept H259-H263 as dataset-specific fast-growth context support for the six main axes and close them. Residual concerns remain that fast-growth eligibility is a measured, correlated phenotype and these are not external validations, but the effect sizes are too large for those concerns to overturn the in-dataset conclusion. The receptor co-dependency tests are null. H264/R235 estimates +0.0004 for ERBB2-amplification associated EGFR dependency among EGFR-amplification-negative lines, with a null interval and negligible magnitude. H265/R236 estimates -0.0117, opposite the registered direction and imprecise. I reject H264 and H265. These are dataset-specific lack-of-association results, not proof that RTK dependency cannot be context dependent elsewhere. H266/R237 tests RB1 loss as a direct STAT3 predictor and gives +0.0386, with a 95% interval of +0.0032 to +0.0740. This supports a small positive association with stronger STAT3 dependency in RB1-loss lines, but the lower bound is close to null and the effect is much smaller than the dominant PTEN-loss STAT3 axis. Given multiplicity, the modest magnitude, and the possibility that RB1 loss partially tracks with other pathway lesions such as PTEN loss, I leave H266 unresolved and active, and register a PTEN-intact restricted direct test and an RB1-by-PTEN interaction test to assess whether the signal is independent of the dominant PTEN-loss STAT3 association. The interaction panel does not support meaningful context modification except for a borderline serum effect. H267/R238, an attenuating CDKN2A-loss-by-fast-growth interaction for MDM2 dependency, estimates -0.045 with a null interval; no evidence of attenuation is established, and the accepted fast-growth main effect remains. H268/R239, a PTEN-loss-by-fast-growth interaction for STAT3 dependency, is near zero and imprecise, again supporting robustness of the parent axis rather than fast-growth modification. H270/R241, a SMARCA4-loss-by-serum-rich interaction for SMARCA2 dependency, has a small positive interval crossing zero, so no evidence for serum-dependent attenuation or enhancement. I reject these interaction claims as directional claims because their intervals include zero and the parent main effects are already accepted. H269/R240, KEAP1-loss-by-serum-rich interaction for NFE2L2 dependency, is statistically positive but small, +0.043 with lower bound near null. It may indicate a slight enhancement of the KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 association in serum-rich culture, but the magnitude is minor relative to the very large main effect and the interval is not robust enough to accept as a clinically or mechanistically important modifier. I leave it unresolved but closed, given that the main KEAP1-NFE2L2 association is already robust and further effort is better spent on the unresolved RB1-STAT3 follow-up. No validation is requested because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. These conclusions are limited to the supplied dataset; they are not claims about causality, synthetic lethality, therapeutic vulnerability, or generalization.","synthesize":"No assessments were due and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so no new validation was requested. I assessed all validation evidence present in the ledger against the registered hypothesis direction, interpreting returned estimates exactly as already signed and not applying any additional sign transformation. The central conclusion is that the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR screen dataset contains several large, reproducible, dataset-specific genotype dependency associations, while many direct matched-gene dependency hypotheses and effect-modifier hypotheses are absent or too uncertain to support. Six main axes are well supported. The interaction direction is deliberately chosen to match the accepted parent axis for that outcome. Therefore, after sign conversion, a positive signed estimate means the exposure-comparator dependency difference is enhanced in the subgroup relative to its complement, whereas a negative signed estimate means attenuation. An interval excluding zero would provide evidence for context modification; an interval centered near zero would support robustness of the parent axis in that context. The CDKN2A-loss MDM2 fast-growth interaction asks whether the accepted CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 dependency persists with the same magnitude in faster-growing lines. H259/R230 gives a signed effect of +0.759 for SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency in faster-growing lines, with a tight interval that excludes null and a magnitude far above any plausible 10% relevance threshold. H260/R231 gives +0.807 for TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 dependency under the same growth-rate eligibility. H261/R232 gives +0.814 for KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, consistent with the accepted direction. H262/R233 gives +0.288 for PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, similar to the accepted main and validated effect. H263/R234 gives +0.776 for MSI-high stronger WRN dependency. These effects are large relative to the scale of the corresponding dependency scores, have stable cell counts, and are inconsistent with mere chance. I therefore accept H259-H263 as dataset-specific fast-growth context support for the six main axes and close them. Residual concerns remain that fast-growth eligibility is a measured, correlated phenotype and these are not external validations, but the effect sizes are too large for those concerns to overturn the in-dataset conclusion. The receptor co-dependency tests are null. H264/R235 estimates +0.0004 for ERBB2-amplification associated EGFR dependency among EGFR-amplification-negative lines, with a null interval and negligible magnitude. H265/R236 estimates -0.0117, opposite the registered direction and imprecise. I reject H264 and H265. These are dataset-specific lack-of-association results, not proof that RTK dependency cannot be context dependent elsewhere. H266/R237 tests RB1 loss as a direct STAT3 predictor and gives +0.0386, with a 95% interval of +0.0032 to +0.0740. This supports a small positive association with stronger STAT3 dependency in RB1-loss lines, but the lower bound is close to null and the effect is much smaller than the dominant PTEN-loss STAT3 axis. record.narrative:
No assessments are due and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore step does not alter accept/reject conclusions and does not request independent validation. It activates four previously registered, high-value unresolved direct co-genotype or predictor claims: H49 tests whether the strong TP53-wildtype stronger USP7 association persists specifically within KEAP1-loss lines; H51 tests whether the strong KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 association persists specifically within TP53-loss lines; H144 tests whether TP53-wildtype versus TP53-loss changes MDM2 dependency within CDKN2A-loss lines, clarifying whether the accepted CDKN2A-loss MDM2 axis depends on TP53 status; and H151 tests MTAP-loss as a direct STAT3 predictor. These status changes are investigation prioritization only, not evidence-based acceptance.

The six new discovery proposals use binary genotype exposures and measured binary or continuous eligibility contexts to avoid the earlier invalid continuous-exposure threshold coding. Each returned estimate must be interpreted exactly as already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 main effects, a positive signed value supports raw more-negative dependency in the exposed group, i.e. stronger dependency. For direction +1 NFE2L2 effects, a positive signed value supports raw less-negative dependency in KEAP1-loss lines, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Context tests ask whether an accepted dataset-specific association retains its magnitude in a specified measured context; they are not causal or therapeutic claims.

The RB1-loss STAT3 claim restricted to CDKN2A-intact lines extends the small H266 signal by testing whether it persists outside CDKN2A-loss lines. If replicated with the same direction and meaningful magnitude, it would favor an independent dataset-specific RB1-loss association. If null or reversed, the H266 signal becomes more likely fragile or correlated with other genomic lesions. The MTAP-loss STAT3 claim restricted to PTEN-intact lines tests whether MTAP loss has any STAT3 association independent of the much stronger PTEN-loss STAT3 axis; anticipated direction is deliberately uncertain because H151 has no direct evidence. The serum-rich eligibility tests for CDKN2A-loss MDM2, TP53-wildtype USP7, and PTEN-loss STAT3 ask whether the accepted magnitudes persist under a high-serum culture state rather than being diluted by medium-related biology. The high-hypoxia KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 direct main effect complements earlier interaction testing by estimating the full magnitude in a hypoxia-enriched context, where oxidative-stress pathway relationships might be attenuated or enhanced. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations among measured lung-lineage cell-line features.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All new estimates are read exactly as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. A positive signed value for direction -1 means raw stronger dependency in the exposed or TP53-wild-type group; for direction +1 NFE2L2 claims, a positive signed value means raw weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. H49 and H51 are very strong co-genotype context tests. In KEAP1-loss lines, TP53-wild-type versus TP53-loss has signed estimate +0.794, 95% interval +0.754 to +0.834, closely matching the parent TP53-wild-type stronger USP7 association; I accept H49 and close it as a robust within-KEAP1-loss context. In TP53-loss lines, KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact has signed estimate +0.810, interval +0.763 to +0.857, consistent with the parent KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 association; I accept H51. H144 asks whether TP53-wild-type status changes MDM2 dependency within CDKN2A-loss lines. The signed estimate is only +0.015, interval -0.067 to +0.097. This is neither meaningful nor precise enough to support a TP53 context effect inside CDKN2A-loss, so I reject H144. This does not challenge the accepted CDKN2A-loss MDM2 axis; earlier TP53-intact and TP53-loss strata already indicated persistence across TP53 status. H151 and H274 reject MTAP loss as a STAT3 predictor: the whole-sample direct estimate is opposite the hypothesis direction and imprecise, and the PTEN-intact restricted estimate remains near null and crosses zero. The RB1-loss STAT3 follow-up is more subtle. H271, restricted to PTEN-intact lines, gives +0.031 with interval +0.004 to +0.057. H273, restricted to CDKN2A-intact lines, gives +0.046 with interval +0.004 to +0.088. Both are directionally consistent and statistically separated from null, but both are small relative to the dominant PTEN-loss STAT3 axis and the practical threshold used in this run; the lower bounds are very close to zero and many correlated genomic features raise multiplicity and confounding concerns. H272, the RB1-by-PTEN-loss interaction, is null and very wide, so there is no evidence that RB1 loss modifies the PTEN-loss STAT3 association. I therefore reject the interaction claim but leave H271, H273, and the parent H266 unresolved as possible modest dataset-specific RB1 associations. I close the line because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted and further effort is better directed to accepted-axis robustness. The serum-rich culture context strongly supports the main accepted axes: CDKN2A-loss MDM2 +0.114, interval +0.070 to +0.157; TP53-wild-type USP7 +0.800, interval +0.774 to +0.826; PTEN-loss STAT3 +0.286, interval +0.216 to +0.357. I accept and close H275, H276, and H277. The high-hypoxia KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 direct main effect is also robust, +0.754, interval +0.711 to +0.797, so H278 is accepted and closed. No validation is requested because the remaining new voluntary validation capacity is zero. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causality, synthetic lethality, therapeutic vulnerability, or external generalization.

4. KEAP1 loss is strongly associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Core claim H17/R6 gives estimate 0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R26 estimate 0.800, interval 0.772 to 0.829. The sign means KEAP1-loss lines are less negative on dependency_NFE2L2, i.e. weaker dependency. It is robust in adenocarcinoma H20/R16, TP53-intact and TP53-loss lines H31/R169 and H51/R247, fast growth H261/R232, KRAS-mutant lines H234/R209, ploidy strata H211/R197 and H250/R221, screen-quality subsets H61/R50, H62/R51, H176/R151, H186/R161, H205/R185, MTAP-loss lines H168/R143, and high hypoxia H278/R253.

5. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Core claim H81/R63 gives estimate 0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R66 estimate 0.310, interval 0.231 to 0.388. This effect is much larger than the 10% practical benchmark and is robust across batch H84/R67, Cas9 eligibility H85/R68, adherent culture H86/R69, adenocarcinoma H87/R70, PIK3CA-intact and mutant lines H90/R73 and H106/R85 plus validation R107, high and low IFN-gamma strata H91/R74 and H102/R81, TP53-intact and loss strata H169/R144 and H107/R86, KRAS-mutant lines H230/R203, fast growth H262/R233, EMT and AXL-high contexts H227/R201, H228/R202, H248/R219, low ploidy H252/R223, and serum-rich media H277/R252.

6. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Core claim H132/R119 gives estimate 0.117, interval 0.082 to 0.152, validated by R120 estimate 0.100, interval 0.049 to 0.151. The point estimate is about 43% of the mean MDM2 dependency magnitude in this dataset, clearly exceeding the 10% benchmark. It persists across TP53-intact and loss strata H134/R121 and H135/R122, MTAP-intact and combined TP53/MTAP-intact eligibility H138/R125 and H147/R135, KRAS-mutant lines H231/R204, ploidy and aneuploidy strata H213/R199, H253/R224, H150/R152, growth-rate eligibility H247/R218 and H174/R149, screen-quality halves H226/R200 and H229/R206, and serum-rich media H275/R250.

NEGATIVE FINDINGS. The dataset rejects many straightforward matched-gene dependency hypotheses. BRAF V600E is not associated with stronger BRAF dependency, H1/R1 and H179/R154. KRAS mutation is not associated with stronger KRAS dependency, H6/R4, with near-null validated contrast R80. EGFR amplification is not associated with stronger EGFR dependency in the main or constrained contexts, H3/R2, H18/R14, H33/R24, and H128/R118. ERBB2 amplification is not associated with stronger ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency, H4/R3, H14/R25, and H127/R117. MYC amplification is not associated with stronger DHX9, KIF18A, RPL11, or MDM2 dependency, H2/R108, H5/R109, H11/R110, and H214/R188. TP53 loss itself is not associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, H7/R5; instead CDKN2A loss is the relevant positive association.

The data also reject receptor cross-dependency logic and several secondary direct predictors. ERBB2 amplification is not associated with EGFR dependency among EGFR-amplification-negative lines, H264/R235, and EGFR amplification is not associated with ERBB2 dependency among ERBB2-amplification-negative lines, H265/R236. PIK3CA mutation does not support the registered EGFR, ERBB2, KRAS, or MDM2 dependency hypotheses, H255-R256, H256-R257, H257-R258, and H258-R229. PTEN loss does not support dependency_WRN, RPL11, EGFR, ERBB2, KRAS, or MDM2, H219/R191, H190/R171, H122/R112, H121/R111, H89/R72, and H93/R76. KEAP1 loss does not support dependency_WRN or USP7, H218/R190 and H74/R56. ARID1A loss does not support dependency_SMARCA2 or WRN, H19/R15 and H235/R205. RB1 loss does not support dependency_MDM2 or KIF18A, H191/R172 and H116/R102. The constructed research markers D, E, and F show no meaningful associations, H45-R35 through H48/R38. Additional negative direct tests include MTAP loss against STAT3, H151/R249 and H274/R245, and many near-null or opposite-direction estimates across the 16 outcomes.

UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY. Several secondary signals remain unresolved rather than accepted or rejected. Discovery-positive interaction or subgroup claims that did not survive independent validation include H92/R75 with validation R79, H103/R82 with validation R93, H120/R100 with validation R106, and H139/R126 with validation R133. H195/R176 is an EMT-interaction signal, but direct PTEN-loss STAT3 strata are robust, making this low priority. H207/R187 is an unresolved question about whether very-high screen-quality filtering attenuates CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency; broad screen-quality halves H226/R200 and H229/R206 do not challenge the main axis. H269/R240 is a small borderline serum-rich KEAP1 interaction; the core KEAP1-NFE2L2 association is large and robust, so this modifier remains closed as unresolved.

The most biologically interesting unresolved secondary predictor is RB1 loss for STAT3 dependency. Whole-sample claim H266/R237 gives signed estimate 0.0386, interval 0.0032 to 0.0740. PTEN-intact restricted H271/R242 gives 0.0309, interval 0.0043 to 0.0574, and CDKN2A-intact restricted H273/R244 gives 0.0458, interval 0.0039 to 0.0877. These are directionally consistent and exclude the null, but the point estimates are only modest relative to the practical threshold and lower bounds are very close to zero; with many correlated genomic features and no validation capacity remaining, I keep them unresolved as possible small dataset-specific associations rather than accept them. H272/R243, the RB1-by-PTEN-loss interaction for STAT3, is null and wide, so RB1 loss does not appear to modify the PTEN-loss STAT3 association.

Technical unresolved cases include claims H236-H243 and likely H244-H246. These failed because continuous-threshold exposure coding produced insufficient cells, not because the biology was tested and rejected. They should be re-formulated with valid binary or eligibility-based coding before scientific conclusions are drawn about continuous expression, hypoxia, growth-rate, or SLFN11 thresholds.

MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS. Because independent validation capacity is exhausted, the best next step is discovery-level completion of the registered low-serum robustness tests H279, H280, H281, and H282: PTEN-loss STAT3, TP53-wild-type USP7, CDKN2A-loss MDM2, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency among lines with media_serum_pct <= 5. These test whether the accepted serum-rich persistence is not a one-context artifact and whether the six main axes are robust across a low-serum culture state. If all four remain directionally consistent and meaningful, the accepted axes become more culture-context robust. If any are strongly attenuated, that indicates measured culture-state dependence rather than refuting the core associations. Secondary priority is to re-formulate continuous-threshold predictors with valid comparisons; otherwise, further analysis should prioritize context robustness of the six accepted axes rather than small secondary predictors.

LIMITATIONS. All conclusions are associations in this supplied dataset only. Screen features, library/batch, Cas9 activity, doubling time, ploidy, subtype, growth rate, media, and co-genotype correlations can confound apparent dependency associations. Validation strengthens in-dataset replication but does not establish causality, synthetic lethality, drug vulnerability, or generalization to other cohorts or experimental systems.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity remains exhausted, so this explore step does not change any accept/reject conclusion and does not request validation. It instead completes the most informative remaining robustness program: direct culture-medium context tests for the six accepted dataset-specific dependency axes. Four low-serum main-effect claims are already active for PTEN-loss STAT3, TP53-wild-type USP7, CDKN2A-loss MDM2, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2. This iteration adds the missing media context claims for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2, MSI-high WRN, and a direct serum-rich KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 main effect. It also registers two low-versus-complement interaction tests for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 and MSI-high WRN to quantify culture-state dependence rather than merely estimate each context separately. These are not new causal claims; they test whether an accepted in-dataset association remains present and comparable across measured culture states. Returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 main effects, a positive signed value supports raw stronger dependency, i.e. more-negative dependency, in the exposed or TP53-wild-type group. For direction +1 NFE2L2 effects, a positive signed value supports raw weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. less-negative dependency, in KEAP1-loss lines. For interactions, positive signed values support an enhanced contrast under the registered hypothesis direction in the low-serum subgroup relative to its complement; negative signed values support attenuation or reversal in low serum relative to complement. A null or attenuated low-serum result would indicate measured context dependence, not refutation of the broader dataset-specific axis, whereas a similarly large low-serum effect would strengthen the claim that these associations are not artifacts of the high-serum subset. All conclusions remain limited to this supplied 2000-line dataset and do not establish causality, synthetic lethality, therapeutic vulnerability, or external generalizability.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
